The ideal candidate will have extensive experience with critical electrical systems, operational best practices, electrical safety, switching procedures, energized work controls, and critical environment procedures. Review electrical designs for operability, maintainability, reliability, resiliency, redundancy, and compliance with client operational standards. Participate in design reviews, constructability reviews, commissioning readiness reviews, operational readiness assessments, project meetings, and technical workshops. Evaluate electrical system performance, operational risk, redundancy strategies, switching sequences, failure modes, maintenance bypass arrangements, and reliability objectives. Prepare clear and technically accurate documentation, including engineering reports, risk assessments, operating procedures, technical evaluations, and review comments. QUALIFICATIONS Required qualifications: 10+ years of experience in electrical engineering, electrical operations, commissioning, mission-critical engineering, facility operations, or comparable technical environments. Minimum 5+ years of direct data center or critical facilities operations experience. Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Strong understanding of electrical infrastructure supporting critical facilities and Tier III / Tier IV data centers. Demonstrated experience developing, reviewing, and validating SOPs, EOPs, and MOPs. Strong technical knowledge of utility service, MV/LV distribution, switchgear, transformers, UPS systems, STS, ATS, PDUs, RPPs, busway systems, emergency generators, generator paralleling systems, BESS, grounding and bonding systems, protective relaying, and power monitoring systems. Experience evaluating electrical systems for operational risk, redundancy, resiliency, maintainability, reliability, and compliance with operational requirements. Working knowledge of mission-critical industry standards, codes, and operational best practices, including ASHRAE, NFPA, ISO, IEC, Uptime Institute Tier Standards, TIA-942, BICSI, IBC, IFC, IECC, local authority requirements, and other applicable international standards. Ability to apply engineering standards to real-world data center design, commissioning, operations, maintenance, operational readiness, and emergency response. Strong understanding of change management, Permit-to-Work systems, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), energized electrical work procedures, switching procedures, risk assessments, incident response, root cause analysis, preventive maintenance, reliability-centered maintenance (RCM), and continuous improvement. Excellent technical writing, documentation, communication, and presentation skills. Ability to work effectively with clients, contractors, commissioning authorities, facility operations teams, and multidisciplinary project teams. Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, organizational, and time management skills. Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Preferred qualifications: Direct experience supporting mission-critical facilities in Saudi Arabia or the broader GCC region. Experience supporting hyperscale data centers such as AWS, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, or similar environments. Experience with colocation providers such as QTS, Equinix, Digital Realty, Compass Datacenters, Vantage, Aligned, STACK Infrastructure, CyrusOne, or similar operators. Minimum 5+ years of project or program management experience leading complex, multidisciplinary technical projects. Professional Engineer (PE), Chartered Engineer status, or equivalent professional registration. Experience serving as a Commissioning Authority (CxA), Owner’s Engineer, Owner’s Representative, or client-side technical advisor. Experience supporting Tier III or Tier IV data center operations, commissioning, operational readiness, electrical procedure validation, or electrical reliability programs. Professional certifications related to data centers, electrical safety, commissioning, operations, or project management are preferred. JOB_TITLE: CNC Coolant Filling Technician - PWHT Plants Experience
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Eram Talent is seeking a detail-oriented and highly skilled CNC Coolant Filling Technician with specific experience in Post Weld Heat Treatment (PWHT) plant environments. The successful candidate will be responsible for the comprehensive management, preparation, and maintenance of metalworking fluids and coolants for high-precision CNC machinery. This role is critical to maximizing tool life, ensuring machining quality, and maintaining safe, continuous operations within a heavy industrial setting. Key Responsibilities Coolant Management: Accurately mix, distribute, and replenish coolants, cutting fluids, and lubricants across multiple CNC machines according to specific operational parameters. System Testing & Monitoring: Perform daily chemical tests using refractometers and pH meters to monitor coolant concentration, alkalinity, and biological control. Equipment Maintenance: Execute routine cleaning of machine sumps, operate tramp oil skimmers, and maintain coolant recycling and filtration equipment to prevent fluid degradation. PWHT Plant Integration: Safely navigate and operate within heavy industrial environments, specifically alongside Post Weld Heat Treatment (PWHT) operations, ensuring all fluid management aligns with the plant's production and heat-treating schedules. Troubleshooting: Identify and resolve fluid-related issues such as foaming, foul odors, rust, or poor tool life, adjusting chemical dosing as necessary. Position Overview: The Senior Manufacturing Test Engineer – Inverter will play a lead role in developing, launching, and sustaining automated test systems for Lucid’s electric traction inverter manufacturing lines. This role is critical to EV power electronics production and focuses on in‑process and end‑of‑line (EOL) testing of high‑voltage inverters to ensure functional performance, safety, efficiency, and long‑term reliability. The engineer will work closely with Design Engineering, Controls, Quality, Production, and external equipment suppliers to deliver robust, scalable, and data‑driven inverter test solutions. Responsibilities: Review and approve inverter test specifications and change requests from design engineering, acting as the manufacturing test authority for traction inverter validation. Analyze and provide feedback on test sequences, limits, cycle time, process flow, and failure‑mode handling for inverter EOL and sub‑assembly test stations. Design and own test system hardware for inverter testing, including system layout, cabinet and rack design, HV/LV routing, connectorization, shielding, grounding, and thermal considerations for high‑power switching electronics. Develop modular and scalable test applications with clear operator interfaces for inverter testing, including parameter management, test sequencing, fault messaging, and data logging. Implement databases to manage inverter test parameters, serial‑level results, traceability, and correlation to manufacturing and quality systems. Define DUT handling, fixturing, and electrical/mechanical interfaces for inverter test stations, including automated HV connections and safety interlocks. Collaborate with controls engineers to integrate test applications with station PLCs, dynos or load systems, cooling systems, and material handling equipment, including responses to electrical, thermal, and safety‑critical failure modes. Lead sourcing, RFQs, supplier selection, build tracking, and technical oversight for externally supplied inverter test equipment. Develop and execute commissioning and validation plans for inverter test systems, including GR&R, red‑rabbit units, fault injection, and simulation of electrical, thermal, and communication failures. Launch inverter test systems into production and provide on‑floor support during ramp, including limit tuning, yield improvement, and false‑fail reduction. Train maintenance and operations teams on inverter test station operation, error recovery, and safe troubleshooting of high‑voltage power electronics. Partner with factory data and analytics teams to enable inverter test data visualization, yield tracking, efficiency trends, and long‑term quality monitoring. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s Degree in Controls Systems Engineering, Electrical and Controls Engineering, or Automation and Control Engineering and at least 5 years of professional experience 5~8 years of experience developing and launching automated test equipment in high‑volume manufacturing environments. Direct experience testing EV traction inverters or high‑power power electronics in a manufacturing or production setting. Strong understanding of inverter architectures, power stages, gate drivers, DC‑link capacitors, current sensing, and thermal management. Hands‑on experience with inverter EOL and in‑process testing such as functional power testing, PWM validation, phase current measurement, switching performance, efficiency testing, isolation resistance, and hipot testing. Detailed knowledge of high‑voltage and high‑current electrical components, connectors, cables, shielding, and grounding best practices. Ability to design electrical schematics using AutoCAD, EPLAN, or equivalent tools. Experience developing test hardware using National Instruments platforms such as PXI, cDAQ, or cRIO. Skills: Strong software development experience with NI LabVIEW, NI TestStand, Python, MATLAB, or similar tools used in manufacturing test environments. Working knowledge of automotive communication protocols including CAN, CAN‑FD, LIN, and Automotive Ethernet, including inverter diagnostics and calibration interfaces. Proficiency using electrical test equipment such as power supplies, electronic loads, oscilloscopes, DMMs, power analyzers, and inverter or power electronics diagnostic tools. Experience interfacing test systems with PLCs and industrial networks such as Ethernet/IP or OPC‑UA is a plus. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple inverter test stations, suppliers, and launch timelines in parallel. Clear and professional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, production, quality, and external suppliers. Proven job knowledge to handle operational responsibilities on critical wells as outlined above and demonstrated personnel attributes of sound judgment, dependability, honest work ethic and leadership.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: About Us Tamara is a leading fintech platform in Saudi Arabia and the GCC region with a mission to help people own their dreams built on being simple, trusted, and everywhere our customers need us. Your Role The Head of AML will lead and manage the overall operations, activities, and responsibilities of the AML/CTF Department, reporting administratively to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and functionally to the Audit Committee. The role is responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining the company’s Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing, and Proliferation Financing (AML/CTF/PF) framework in Saudi Arabia. This includes ensuring compliance with the Saudi Anti-Money Laundering Law and its Implementing Regulations, SAMA requirements, SAFIU reporting obligations, and applicable Targeted Financial Sanctions requirements. The Head of AML will work closely with business and control functions to identify and assess financial-crime risks, ensure that effective controls are implemented consistently across the company, remediate identified gaps, and promote a strong culture of AML/CTF/PF compliance. Your Responsibilities AML/CTF/PF Framework and Controls: Develop, implement, monitor, and continuously enhance the company’s AML/CTF/PF framework and controls to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with applicable regulatory requirements. Oversight of AML/CTF/PF Operations: Lead and oversee the AML/CTF Unit’s activities, ensuring that all responsibilities are performed effectively and that identified control or process deficiencies are addressed promptly. Policies and Procedures: Develop, maintain, and periodically review the company’s AML/CTF/PF policies, procedures, standards, and operating controls to reflect regulatory developments, emerging risks, and relevant industry practices. Enterprise-Wide Risk Assessment: Oversee the identification and assessment of money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing risks arising from the company’s customers, products, services, transactions, delivery channels, and geographic exposure. Stakeholder Management and Advisory: Build and maintain effective relationships with key internal stakeholders and provide guidance and advice on AML/CTF/PF risks, regulatory requirements, new products, business initiatives, and control enhancements. Sanctions and PEP Screening: Oversee sanctions, Targeted Financial Sanctions, and politically exposed person screening controls, including alert investigation, escalation, decision-making, freezing measures, and regulatory reporting where applicable. Board and Senior Management Reporting: Provide the CEO and Audit Committee with regular reports on the company’s AML/CTF/PF risk exposure, control effectiveness, key performance indicators, material cases, regulatory developments, identified deficiencies, and the status of remediation actions. Stakeholder Management and Advisory: Build and maintain effective relationships with key internal stakeholders and provide guidance, awareness, and advice on AML/CTF/PF risks, requirements, and controls. Transaction Monitoring & Alert Management: Oversee transaction monitoring mechanisms ensuring effective rule tuning, threshold settings, and scenario management to minimize false positives. Suspicious Activity Reporting: Ensure that unusual activities are investigated appropriately and that suspicious transaction or activity reports are submitted accurately, confidentially, and within the applicable timelines to the Saudi Financial Intelligence Unit through official reporting channels. Regulatory Engagement: Act as the primary point of contact for AML/CTF/PF matters and coordinate timely, accurate, and complete responses to requests, inspections, and inquiries from SAMA, SAFIU, and other competent authorities. Team Leadership: Manage and develop the AML/CTF team, establish clear responsibilities and performance expectations, and ensure the function has appropriate resources, knowledge, systems, and capabilities. Your expertise At least 6 + years of relevant experience in AML/CTF, financial-crime compliance, regulatory compliance, or a related field, including experience in a leadership or management role under SAMA supervision. Previously approved / pre-approved by SAMA is highly desirable, but not mandatory. Strong knowledge of the Saudi AML/CTF regulatory framework, SAMA requirements, SAFIU reporting obligations, Targeted Financial Sanctions, and relevant international standards. Extensive experience in transaction monitoring, alert and case management, suspicious activity investigations, sanctions screening, and AML system capabilities. Strong understanding of money laundering, terrorist financing, and proliferation financing risks, typologies, red flags, and control practices. leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills. Strong leadership, analytical, decision-making, communication, and stakeholder-management skills. Ability to handle sensitive and confidential matters with sound judgment, independence, and integrity. Relevant professional certification, such as CAMS, an ICA qualification, or an equivalent financial-crime compliance certification. The Business Analyst Venture Building role is a strategic catalyst for turning market signals into validated growth opportunities. Your insights will inform prioritization and guide the strategic roadmap for new ventures within the organization. Rapid prototyping and experimentation are at the core of your approach. You will define learning agendas with clear hypotheses, success criteria, and test plans, and you will partner with design and engineering to rapid prototype MVPs, pilots, or low fidelity experiments that produce measurable data. What you will bring includes a bachelor's degree in business, economics, engineering, or a related field and 4 to 7 years of experience in business analysis, strategy, product analytics, corporate development, or management consulting. You are proficient with market sizing, scenario planning, and financial modeling and comfortable using tools such as Excel or Sheets, SQL, or data visualization platforms. You communicate clearly and persuasively, can influence without authority, and thrive in fast paced environments with ambiguity. You are a collaborative teammate who enjoys working with product, design, and engineering to turn insights into impact. We offer a dynamic and inclusive culture that values curiosity, experimentation, and data driven decision making. You will join a high energy cross functional team and have opportunities to grow into product leadership or venture founder tracks, with exposure to multiple markets and business models. We provide competitive compensation, equity options where applicable, comprehensive benefits, flexible work arrangements, and a commitment to professional development through mentoring and ongoing learning. If you are excited to build and validate new ventures from first principles and to influence product strategy through rigorous analysis and rapid prototyping, we encourage you to apply. Evaluate maintenance frequencies, procedures, staffing levels, contract scopes, and resource allocation. Monitor PPM compliance performance across all hospitality assets. Establish technical governance frameworks and maintenance performance reporting structures. Assess requests against asset condition, lifecycle requirements, risk mitigation needs, statutory obligations, operational priorities, and return on investment. Ensure POMEC investments support asset preservation and long-term value creation. Monitor approved capital expenditure implementation and project close-out. Engineering & Building Systems Governance Establish technical standards and engineering governance frameworks across the hospitality portfolio. Review performance of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire and life safety, BMS, ELV, vertical transportation, water treatment, and specialist hospitality systems. Ensure critical systems operate safely, efficiently, and in accordance with applicable regulations and standards. Review technical risks associated with aging infrastructure, deferred maintenance, operational changes, and capital interventions. Support development of technical policies, engineering standards, and asset management procedures. Sustainability & Resource Management Support implementation of sustainability initiatives across the portfolio. Review building performance data relating to energy, water, waste, and carbon reduction opportunities. Identify technical initiatives that improve operational efficiency and environmental performance. Support compliance with sustainability frameworks including LEED, BREEAM, Green Key, GRESB, and relevant Saudi sustainability requirements. Promote energy management, utility optimization, and lifecycle efficiency practices. Review asset condition surveys, engineering audits, lifecycle assessments, and risk analyses. Identify technical risks and recommend mitigation plans. Ensure asset management decisions are supported by technical data and lifecycle considerations. Advise Asset Management leadership on technical implications of investment, operational, and capital expenditure decisions. Stakeholder Management & Governance Act as the primary owner-side technical representative with hotel operators, FM providers, consultants, contractors, project teams, and internal stakeholders. Support technical reviews with operators and engineering leadership teams. Present technical recommendations and risk assessments to senior management. Ensure technical recommendations are supported by engineering rationale, financial analysis, asset preservation requirements, and operational impact assessments. Coordinate closely with Asset Management, Development, Operational Readiness, Finance, Legal, Procurement, and Sustainability teams. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, Facilities Management, or related discipline. Professional Engineering registration or equivalent certification preferred. Minimum 15 years of professional experience. Minimum 10 years within hospitality engineering, hotel technical services, facilities management, or asset management. Experience overseeing luxury hotels, resorts, mixed-use developments, or large integrated destinations. Demonstrated experience leading hotel handovers, commissioning reviews, operational readiness, and defect management. Proven experience reviewing PPM programs, maintenance strategies, and engineering governance frameworks. Strong understanding of POMEC planning, lifecycle asset management, and technical capital expenditure evaluation. Experience working with international hotel operators and hospitality brands. GCC and large-scale destination development experience strongly preferred. Preferred Skills Strong technical understanding of hotel building systems and engineering operations. Expertise in lifecycle asset management and capital planning. Advanced knowledge of maintenance management methodologies. Ability to challenge operators and consultants constructively while maintaining collaborative relationships. Strong analytical and problem-solving capability. Experience interpreting technical drawings, commissioning documentation, and engineering reports. Financial understanding of POMEC, CAPEX, lifecycle costing, and ROI assessments. Excellent stakeholder management and presentation skills. Strong governance, risk management, and compliance mindset. Ability to translate technical issues into commercial and operational implications. KPIs / Success Measures Successful handover of hospitality assets with minimal operational defects or technical disruptions. Completion of technical readiness reviews prior to hotel openings. PPM compliance maintained above established portfolio targets. Reduction in critical equipment failures and asset downtime across the portfolio. POMEC submissions reviewed and approved within established timelines. Capital projects delivered in accordance with approved scope, budget, and technical requirements. Technical audit findings resolved within agreed corrective action periods. Asset lifecycle plans developed and maintained for all operating assets. Improvement in utility efficiency and sustainability performance metrics. Reduction in maintenance backlog and deferred maintenance exposure. Effective management of warranty claims, defects, and technical risk mitigation programs. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Governance • Build, lead, and develop the risk and security team. • Present regular risk and security posture updates to executive leadership and the board/risk committee. • Manage relationships with regulators, auditors, and external security partners. • Own the risk and security budget, tooling, and roadmap. What Are We Looking For❓ • Bachelor’s degree in information security, Risk Management, Computer Science, or related field (Master's preferred) • 10+ years of experience in risk management and/or cybersecurity, with 5+ years in a leadership role. • Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, or equivalent. • Strong knowledge of regulatory frameworks relevant to the industry/region. • Proven experience building risk frameworks and security programs from the ground up or scaling existing ones. • Excellent stakeholder management and board-level communication skills • Fluent in English, with strong written and verbal communication skills. Key Competencies • Strategic thinking with hands on execution ability • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills • Crisis management and decision making under pressure • Cross functional influence without direct authority What We Offer You❗ We believe you will love working at Foodics! • We offer highly competitive compensation packages, including bonuses and the potential for shares. • We prioritize personal development and offer regular training and an annual learning stipend to tackle new challenges and grow your career in a hyper-growth environment. • Join a talented team of over 30 nationalities working in 14 countries, and gain valuable experience in an exciting industry. • We offer autonomy, mentoring, and challenging goals that create incredible opportunities for both you and the company.

Payments and know-your-customer fluency as a product problem, not a compliance checkbox: gateway integrations, document flows, and their product implications. Familiarity with Gulf market realities: payment methods, logistics infrastructure, value-added tax and commercial licensing, and how merchant behavior differs across the region. Wheels, Tires & End-of-Line Quality Validation - Serve as technical owner for wheel assemblies, tire fitment, wheel balancing, tire pressure process controls, and assembly variation management. - Support end-of-line vehicle validation activities for chassis-related performance, geometry, handling, and customer satisfaction targets. - Support production launch readiness, issue tracking, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities. Sustaining Engineering - Responsible for the design and development of automative chassis components and assemblies to deliver the highest level of performance in NVH, Durability, and Manufacturability while optimizing cost. - Work closely with other stake owners and attribute owners across the company such as Core engineering. At Salla, we are building the digital backbone of commerce in the region, empowering thousands of merchants to start, grow, and scale their businesses. We turn what's complex into something simple, powerful, and scalable.Catalog is the layer underneath everything. Storefronts, search, recommendations, landing pages, and every channel a merchant sells through all read from the same product data. When it is good, every surface above it gets better at once. When it is thin or wrong, nothing built on top can fix it. Two things make this exciting:. First, Salla does not build the catalog. Merchants do, and often not even the merchant: a freelancer, operations staff, an outsourced agency. Every surface we build inherits what those hands produce. So the question is not how to clean the data. It is how you change what someone produces when they do not work for you and mostly want to finish and move on. Second, no two categories need the same product record. What a fashion merchant needs is not what a pharmacy, a grocer, or a gold merchant needs. The easy answer is to build each category separately, and it does not scale. You will drive impact across five areas The Catalog Engine and Category Setup (one engine, built once, with what each category needs from a product record expressed as configuration rather than code, so supporting one more category is fast and repeatable) Product Data Input (creation, bulk import, editing, and everything that happens at the moment someone types or uploads) Structure and Meaning (taxonomy, attributes, variants, identifiers, normalization, and duplicates) AI Enrichment (extracting and generating product data from what merchants already have, with a clear position on confidence, review, and correction) Downstream Fitness (how this data actually performs where it is consumed: search results, storefronts, recommendations, and external channel feeds) Responsibilities Own the catalog strategy end to end: sequence it into quarters, defend it in the room, and hold it accountable to the numbers it promised. Own the roadmap for how product data gets created and improved on Salla, prioritized on whether the data works downstream rather than on how many fields are filled. Design for the people who actually do the work, including the ones who do not own the store, and make the good path the fastest path rather than a longer one enforced by rules. Keep a new category, a configuration change rather than an engineering project, and be able to show the difference in effort between the first one and the next. Put AI to work where it earns trust: decide what we generate outright, what we suggest for approval, and what we never touch, with a stated confidence policy and a loop that learns from every correction a merchant makes. Define what catalog quality means at Salla and instrument it honestly, tied to the surfaces that consume the data rather than to completeness for its own sake. Own how product data performs in external selling channels, where the requirements are strict and the rejections are visible. Decide how much structure we impose and where merchants stay free, then defend that line against pressure from both directions. Lead 2 to 3 product managers: give them real ownership, coach their framing and craft, run a reliable cadence, and raise the quality bar of what the group ships. Work as one system with the teams that depend on this data: search and discovery, storefronts, vendors, marketplace, and data. Qualifications Six or more years in product management, including work on a self-serve platform where users created their own content or data and you were accountable for the quality of what they produced. A number you owned and moved on that data: completeness that meant something, accuracy, time to publish, adoption of a data tool, or the performance of that data somewhere downstream. Evidence that you changed what users produced at the moment they produced it, rather than cleaning it up afterwards in a pipeline. We will ask which one it was. Platform judgment: you have built something once and made it serve many cases through configuration, and you can explain where you drew the line between what was shared and what was specific, and what you did when it was wrong at scale. AI in production for structured data: extraction, classification, generation, or matching. You can talk concretely about confidence thresholds, error rates, what you let through automatically, and what you did when it was wrong at scale. Literacy in how product data is actually structured: taxonomies, attribute schemas, variants, identifiers, matching and deduplication, and the strict requirements external selling channels impose. You have coached product managers, formally or not, and you are ready to lead a small team without stepping away from the craft yourself. You own outcomes rather than roadmaps, you move quickly through ambiguity, and you build clarity where others see noise. You stay close to the details and you cannot guard your own area, because this data belongs to everyone downstream. Full professional fluency in Arabic and English is required. Merchant context in this region is preferred over theoretical knowledge. Willing to relocate to Saudi Arabia and work on-site. #J-18808-Ljbffr

Department: InfoSec Monitoring Location: KSA Description Tabby creates financial freedom in the way people shop, earn and save by reshaping their relationship with money. Over 17 million users choose Tabby to stay in control of their spending and make the most out of their money. The company’s flagship offering allows shoppers to split their payments online and in-store with no interest or fees. Over 40,000 global brands and small businesses, including Amazon, Noon, IKEA, and SHEIN use Tabby to accelerate growth and gain loyal customers by offering easy and flexible payments online and in stores. Tabby generates over $10 billion in annual transaction volume for its partner brands and is the highest-rated, most-reviewed, largest, and fastest-growing FinTech in the GCC region. Tabby launched in 2019 and has since raised +$1 billion in equity and debt funding from global and regional investors, and is now valued at $4.5 billion. The Cyber Security Analyst (SOC/CTI) is an internal Tabby role responsible for owning and administering Tabby's security operations platform and cyber threat intelligence capability. With 24x7 security monitoring and alert triage delivered by Tabby's managed SOC service provider, the internal SOC/CTI Analyst focuses on the functions Tabby retains in-house: administering Elastic SIEM, managing the Cyble CTI and brand protection platform, governing detection engineering and use case quality, overseeing managed SOC service performance, and serving as the internal authority for incident validation and closure. Working under the guidance of senior SOC engineers and the SOC/CTI Lead, the role ensures Tabby maintains full operational visibility, controls the quality of the managed service, and progressively builds internal SOC and detection engineering expertise aligned to Tabby's Fintech threat landscape. Key Responsibilities SIEM Administration & Log Source Management - Administer Tabby's Elastic SIEM deployment — monitoring platform health, index lifecycle management, cluster performance, and log ingestion rates to maintain continuous operational visibility across all connected log sources. - Own the log source onboarding process — coordinating with IT, Cloud, DevOps, and application teams to integrate new assets into Elastic SIEM via syslog, API connectors, Beats agents, or custom parsers. - Maintain and continuously improve Tabby's asset and log source inventory — tracking onboarding status, ingestion volumes, and coverage gaps, and escalating visibility deficiencies to the SOC Lead for prioritisation. - Perform routine SIEM housekeeping — reviewing index health, managing retention policies, verifying that critical detection rules are active and firing correctly, and resolving parsing errors or dropped log sources promptly. - Support SIEM tuning activities under senior guidance — adjusting field mappings, resolving ingest pipeline issues, and validating that log data is correctly normalised and queryable by the managed SOC team. - Maintain SIEM configuration documentation — recording index patterns, log source integration specifications, agent deployment standards, and platform architecture notes. Detection Engineering & Use Case Governance - Serve as Tabby's internal point of contact for detection engineering — reviewing, testing, and formally approving correlation rules and use cases submitted by the managed SOC provider before production deployment. - Validate detection logic submitted by the vendor — testing use cases against sample log data in a staging environment to confirm accuracy, alignment with Tabby's threat model, and false positive risk before go-live. - Maintain Tabby's use case library — tracking all active, pending, and retired detection rules with their logic, use case ID, last review date, trigger frequency, and approval status. - Monitor weekly use case performance reports from the managed SOC — flagging rules with high false positive rates, untriggered rules, or detection gaps for remediation with the vendor. - Assist in developing Tabby-specific detection requirements for Fintech threats — translating business and regulatory risks (ATO, payment fraud, API abuse, credential stuffing) into detection use case specifications. - Ensure detection coverage aligns with relevant frameworks — reviewing use case libraries against MITRE ATT&CK, SAMA CSF controls, and NCA ECC requirements. Cyber Threat Intelligence & Brand Protection (Cyble) - Administer and manage Tabby's Cyble CTI platform — maintaining platform configuration, user access, feed integrations, and API connectivity between Cyble and the Elastic SIEM environment. - Monitor Cyble for emerging threat intelligence relevant to Tabby — tracking new threat actor TTPs, CVE disclosures targeting Tabby's technology stack, and Fintech-specific threats including ATO campaigns, payment fraud schemes, and mobile app threats. - Manage Tabby's IOC registry — collecting, categorising, and maintaining accurate IOC entries (IP addresses, domains, file hashes, URLs) from Cyble and other feeds, with context, confidence levels, and expiry dates correctly recorded. - Oversee IOC operationalisation — coordinating with the managed SOC team to ensure confirmed IOCs are ingested into Elastic SIEM detection rules within agreed timeframes, and tracking coverage confirmation. - Monitor brand protection alerts via Cyble — reviewing findings for domain spoofing, counterfeit mobile applications, fake social media profiles, dark web data exposure, and leaked credentials; escalating confirmed threats per defined procedures. - Prepare and distribute periodic CTI briefings — compiling notable intelligence findings, brand protection status, active IOC feeds, and sector-relevant threat trends for the SOC Lead and relevant stakeholders. Managed SOC Oversight & Incident Closure - Act as Tabby's primary internal liaison with the managed SOC service provider — reviewing daily alert summaries, weekly threat hunting reports, and monthly management reports submitted by the vendor. - Validate vendor escalations — reviewing incidents escalated by the managed SOC to confirm sufficient investigation evidence, accurate severity classification, and completeness of remediation recommendations before internal action. - Own Tabby's incident closure process — reviewing vendor-recommended closures, confirming remediation actions have been completed, ensuring evidence is properly documented, and formally closing incidents in the incident management system. - Track managed SOC SLA performance — monitoring key metrics including escalation quality, threat hunting deliverable timeliness, and use case update frequency; flagging deviations to the SOC Lead. - Maintain Tabby's incident register — ensuring the master incident log is accurate, current, and audit-ready in line with SAMA CSF and internal governance requirements. - Participate in post-incident reviews — reviewing vendor post-incident reports, validating root cause analysis findings, and tracking agreed corrective actions to completion. SOC Reporting & Continuous Improvement - Maintain SOC operational documentation — escalation records, tool status trackers, runbook libraries, and detection playbooks — ensuring records are accurate, current, and audit-ready. - Support the preparation of SOC performance reports and metrics dashboards — compiling MTTD/MTTR statistics, SLA adherence data, IOC registry accuracy, and use case coverage metrics. - Contribute to SOC process improvement initiatives — identifying gaps in detection coverage, tooling, or process and raising improvement recommendations to the SOC Lead. - Actively invest in continuous self-development — studying SIEM administration, detection engineering, Cyble platform capabilities, and the MITRE ATT&CK framework to build independent expertise and progress toward the next grade. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise - Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related field. - Recent graduates and fresh university leavers are encouraged to apply — no prior professional SOC experience is required. - Academic projects, home labs (e.g., TryHackMe Blue Team paths, HackTheBox, Elastic Stack builds), or internship experience in security operations or monitoring are viewed favorably. - No mandatory professional experience required. Any internship, academic project, or personal lab experience related to security operations, log analysis, SIEM platforms, or threat intelligence is a strong advantage. Hands-on exposure to Elastic Stack, even in a self-study context, is a distinct advantage - Foundational understanding of SIEM platforms — ability to navigate Elastic Stack (Kibana dashboards, KQL/Lucene queries, ESQL) consoles to review alerts, investigate events, and query log data across multiple sources. - Basic understanding of network security fundamentals — TCP/IP protocols, DNS, HTTP/S, common attack traffic patterns (port scans, brute force, C2 beaconing), and how they manifest in SIEM log sources. - Foundational awareness of endpoint security monitoring — Windows Event Log analysis (logon events, process creation, registry changes), Linux syslog, and common persistence and lateral movement indicators.

Renewal Pipeline and Risk-Based Prioritisation · Develop the city-wide lifecycle and renewal pipeline by joining condition, risk, cost, performance, criticality and maintenance data across portfolios. · Prioritise assets coming into operation between 2026 and 2028, ensuring renewal needs, early-life risks and lifecycle obligations are visible before handover. · Set risk-based prioritisation rules that guide when assets are maintained, monitored, refurbished, renewed, replaced or escalated for investment decision. · Create practical rules for transferring lifecycle planning outputs and prioritisation logic to incoming City Operations resources once recruited. · Ensure prioritisation decisions are transparent, evidence-based and auditable, supporting whole-life cost and value optimisation. 3. Intervention Thresholds and Maintenance Policy Integration · Work with asset leads across the wider City AM team to define intervention thresholds, maintenance policies, inspection triggers and asset-specific lifecycle requirements. · Ensure lifecycle planning reflects portfolio-specific asset behaviour, usage intensity, condition profiles, criticality, service impacts and operational constraints. · Translate asset class requirements into consistent planning rules for renewals, planned maintenance, condition monitoring, deterioration assumptions and replacement strategies. · Challenge proposed interventions where cost, risk, performance or lifecycle value are not sufficiently evidenced. · Ensure maintenance and intervention policies remain aligned with operational readiness, O&M feedback, budget planning and long-term asset management objectives. 4. SAP EAMS and Data Integration for Lifecycle Planning · Work with the Enterprise AM Systems / SAP EAMS Director to ensure the AM platform and SAP EAMS are ready to support lifecycle planning, renewal forecasting, intervention rules, condition scoring, risk prioritisation and cost-performance analysis. · Define lifecycle data requirements, including asset hierarchy, classification, condition, criticality, failure modes, replacement value, expected life, maintenance history, cost, risk, performance and renewal information. · Ensure dashboards and reports provide usable outputs for lifecycle forecasts, renewal pipelines, budget inputs, risk registers, backlog visibility, performance trends and portfolio decision-making. · Link asset management outputs to financial reporting and work-management systems to support one version of the truth for lifecycle planning and investment decisions. · Validate that data captured during handover and early operations is sufficient to support lifecycle planning, total cost of ownership, renewal prioritisation and adaptive change management. · Promote a single source of lifecycle asset information that supports balanced decisions over the full lifespan of each asset. 5. Portfolio and Infrastructure Asset Integration · Lead integration of lifecycle planning across asset portfolios, ensuring common AM standards while allowing asset-class specific intervention rules and maintenance policies. · Direct the Asset Lifecycle & Costing Senior Manager to develop lifecycle cost models, renewal forecasts, budget inputs and whole-life cost analysis across asset portfolios. · Direct the Infrastructure Assets Integration Manager to work with the Infrastructure portfolio lead on lifecycle plans and programmes for roads and car parks. · Ensure risks, issues and opportunities from O&M are fed back into prioritisation, lifecycle plans, asset management plans and renewal pipelines. · Coordinate with asset class leads to ensure lifecycle assumptions reflect operational realities, service expectations, deterioration patterns, usage intensity and maintenance strategy. · Provide a city-wide integrated view of asset risk, performance, backlog and lifecycle pressures to inform capital and Opex planning. · Support integrated planning across City AM so lifecycle, costing, risk, criticality, operational integration and infrastructure asset priorities are joined up across the city operating model. 6. Lifecycle Costing, Budget Inputs and Investment Planning · Direct the Asset Lifecycle & Costing Senior Manager to develop lifecycle cost models, renewal forecasts, total cost of ownership analysis and portfolio-level budget inputs. · Translate lifecycle plans into prioritised renewal programmes, multi-year capital requirements and operating budget implications. · Ensure investment recommendations are supported by condition, risk, cost, criticality, performance, backlog and service-impact evidence. · Support capital and Opex planning by identifying short-, medium- and long-term renewal needs, funding risks, deferral impacts and value optimisation options. · Use KPI and trend reporting, performance monitoring and O&M feedback loops to refine lifecycle assumptions, renewal timing and maintenance strategies. · Provide leadership reports on lifecycle cost exposure, renewal priorities, affordability constraints, risks, backlog and value-for-money options. 7. Continuous Improvement and Lifecycle Policy Development · Develop and continuously improve lifecycle planning policies, frameworks, templates, intervention logic, renewal rules, decision criteria and prioritisation methodologies. · Use asset performance monitoring, condition data, risk trends, cost data, O&M feedback, lessons learned and SAP EAMS outputs to refine lifecycle assumptions and planning standards. · Ensure lifecycle planning supports asset monitoring and continuous improvement, including cost, risk and asset health reporting, adaptive change management and lessons learned. · Benchmark lifecycle planning approaches and promote consistency with ISO 55001-aligned asset management principles and relevant international good practice. · Ensure lifecycle frameworks remain practical, scalable and usable by asset leads, O&M teams, portfolio teams and future City Operations resources. · Build lifecycle planning capability across City AM through guidance, workshops, governance routines and clear decision-support tools. JOB_TITLE: Senior Director - Land & Public Realm Optimisation - Land Use (Q - CO)
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Jasara Program Management Company (Jasara PMC) is a leading Joint Venture between Public Investment Fund (PIF), Jacobs, and Saudi Aramco, established to deliver world-class program management services across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Jasara plays a key role in supporting the realization of Saudi Vision 2030, particularly in delivering giga-projects and large-scale infrastructure developments. We are seeking a Senior Director, Land & Public Realm Optimisation - Land Use to join JASARA PMC. The Senior Director, Land & Public Realm Optimisation is accountable for supporting City Operations in reviewing proposed city land and public realm before it is accepted or vested into the City Operations portfolio. The role assesses parks, landscaped areas, plazas, civic spaces, pedestrian areas, green corridors, recreational open spaces and other proposed public land to determine whether each area is genuinely public, operationally necessary, appropriately sized, cost-efficient and financially sustainable throughout its lifecycle. The position acts as City Operations’ independent challenge and assurance function. It provides evidence-based recommendations to the Executive Director, City Operations, and relevant governance forums on whether proposed land should be accepted, conditionally accepted, redesigned, reduced, retained by the benefiting developer or asset owner, placed under an alternative management arrangement, or not vested to City Operations. Key Responsibilities 1. Land and Public Realm Governance · Develop and maintain the City Operations Land and Public Realm Vesting Framework, including review criteria, evidence requirements, stage gates, approval routes and decision records. · Establish consistent standards for determining public purpose, operational need, affordability, maintainability and ownership responsibility. · Ensure proposed land is not assumed to be a City Operations liability solely because it is externally accessible or shown as public realm in a masterplan. · Provide formal recommendations and executive decision papers on acceptance, conditional acceptance, redesign, alternative ownership or rejection. 2. Public Purpose and Beneficiary Assessment · Assess whether proposed land is genuinely public in purpose, access, use and benefit. · Determine whether the primary beneficiaries are the wider city and community or an adjacent private development, hotel, resort, residential community, venue, attraction or commercial asset. · Challenge public designations that do not align with the intended user base, access arrangements or operational reality. · Recommend that land primarily benefiting private assets remains owned, funded or maintained by the benefiting party while protecting any agreed public-access obligations. 3. Land Area and Functional Need Review · Review the scale, location, configuration, boundaries and intended use of parks and other proposed public realm. · Assess whether land area is proportionate to forecast demand, public value and demonstrated operational need. · Challenge oversized, duplicated, fragmented, inaccessible, residual or low-utilisation public spaces. · Identify opportunities to consolidate public realm into fewer, better-performing spaces that provide stronger public value at lower lifecycle cost. · Ensure proposed spaces have a clear function, target user, operating concept and measurable benefit. 4. Parks, Open Space and Public Realm Review · Lead City Operations reviews of public parks, neighbourhood and destination parks, landscaped open areas, urban plazas, civic spaces, pedestrian areas, public squares, green corridors, recreational open spaces and publicly accessible landscaped land. · Assess intended use, forecast demand, opening hours, accessibility, safety, security, thermal comfort, amenities, seasonal use, event potential and long-term renewal needs. · Review landscape intensity, irrigation demand, water use, cleaning, waste, pest control, security patrol, staffing, supervision and maintenance access implications. · Challenge over-designed or maintenance-intensive solutions where simpler alternatives can maintain quality, accessibility and guest experience. 5. Whole-Life Cost and Affordability · Establish a consistent methodology for assessing the whole-life cost of proposed land and public realm. · Prepare or assure annual and long-term cost forecasts covering landscape maintenance, irrigation, water, cleaning, waste, security, pest control, amenities, furniture, play equipment, lighting within public spaces, staffing, technology and periodic renewal. · Compare forecast public value and utilisation with the operating and renewal liability proposed for City Operations. · Identify avoidable cost drivers and recommend redesign, scope reduction, funding contributions or alternative management arrangements where costs are disproportionate. · Maintain clear cost assumptions to support City Operations budget, workforce and service planning. 6. Operational Suitability and Maintainability · Assess whether proposed parks and public spaces can be safely, practically and efficiently operated. · Review access for cleaning, waste collection, landscape maintenance, security patrols, servicing and emergency response. · Identify isolated, concealed, inaccessible or difficult-to-supervise areas and unclear public/private boundaries. · Assess whether landscaping, amenities and materials are suitable for the climate, anticipated use and available maintenance regime. · Recommend design changes that improve usability and reduce cost without undermining public benefit, inclusion or quality. 7. Vesting Recommendations and Conditions · Issue clear recommendations to accept, accept subject to conditions, defer pending evidence, redesign or reduce, retain under developer or asset-owner control, adopt a shared model, or reject from the City Operations portfolio. · Define conditions relating to boundary clarification, design amendments, cost reduction, maintenance funding, service charges, endowments, developer maintenance periods, performance guarantees, public access, handover standards and defect rectification. · Confirm that agreed conditions and required evidence are closed before final acceptance or handover. · Maintain an auditable record of recommendations, decisions, conditions, owners and close-out status. 8. Ownership, Funding and Management Options · Evaluate alternatives to direct vesting, including private ownership with public access, developer-managed public realm, district management, shared maintenance, service-charge recovery, sponsorship, commercial activation, concession or destination-management arrangements. · Ensure alternative models protect public access, service quality, affordability and clear accountability. · Prevent City Operations from assuming costs that should reasonably remain with the principal beneficiary. · Support commercial and legal teams in defining practical ownership, funding and management obligations. 9. Land and Public Realm Portfolio Register · Establish and maintain a citywide register of proposed and accepted public land, recording area, use, beneficiaries, ownership, vesting status, annual operating cost, renewal exposure, risks, funding, conditions and responsible party. · Use the register to identify cumulative cost and workforce exposure across districts and development phases. · Provide executive dashboards on land under review, contested proposals, avoided liabilities, conditional acceptances and future budget exposure. · Support long-term city land optimisation by identifying opportunities to consolidate, reclassify or change management arrangements for underperforming public realm. 10. Stakeholder Coordination and Team Leadership · Lead structured reviews with masterplanning, development, design, landscape architecture, district teams, asset owners, Finance, Commercial, Legal, Governance and City Operations service functions. · Provide early operational input before land boundaries and designs become fixed or commercial commitments are made. · Resolve disagreements concerning public purpose, ownership boundaries, cost and operating responsibility, escalating unresolved issues with evidence and options. · Build and lead a specialist team, supported where required by landscape, cost, land, commercial and operational advisors. · Develop internal guidance and capability so affordability and maintainability are embedded across the development lifecycle. Requirements Education · Bachelor's degree in Urban Planning, Landscape Architecture, Real Estate, Land Economics, Asset Management, Facilities Management, Environmental Design or a related discipline. · Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. · Professional membership in planning, landscape architecture, real estate, asset management or facilities management is desirable. Experience · Minimum 20 years of progressive experience in land-use planning, public realm, parks and open-space planning, landscape planning, real estate, asset management or city operations, including at least 8 years in senior leadership or advisory roles. · Demonstrable experience reviewing parks, public spaces, landscaped areas or major-destination public realm. · Strong experience assessing operating costs, maintenance implications and whole-life liabilities and translating findings into business cases and executive recommendations. · Proven ability to challenge land, design, ownership or funding proposals based on public purpose, operational need, affordability and maintainability. · Experience in Saudi Arabia, the GCC, major destination developments or giga-project environments is strongly preferred. Preferred Background · Experience within a development authority, city or municipal organisation, major destination, integrated resort, public-realm consultancy, real-estate developer or asset-management organisation. · Practical exposure to land vesting, public/private boundary definition, parks operations, landscape maintenance, service-charge models and developer handover. · Experience working across planning, design, operations, finance, commercial, legal and governance disciplines.

ABOUT NASH Nash is last-mile delivery infrastructure. We help the world's largest retailers and commerce companies orchestrate, optimize, and manage their delivery operations. Founded in San Francisco in 2021, backed by Andreessen Horowitz and Y Combinator, Nash works with enterprise customers across North America, Europe, APAC, and the Middle East. Our platform sits at the center of complex delivery operations: connecting carriers, optimizing routes, managing fleets, and giving operators the visibility and control they need to run delivery at scale. We're not a marketplace. We're the infrastructure layer that makes the whole system work. Every enterprise customer presents a different operational reality. A grocery chain running same-day delivery from hundreds of stores has different constraints than a retailer consolidating three carrier networks into one. Nash doesn't sell a fixed product off a price sheet. We design and configure solutions around how each customer actually operates, then deploy with dedicated engineering and product support. The sales process is inseparable from the solution design process. THE OPPORTUNITY Nash has an established Middle East business anchored by strategic enterprise work in Saudi Arabia. We're now at the point where two things need to happen at once: deepen our enterprise footprint in the Kingdom, and prove that Nash's model works across the wider GCC. This role exists to do both. You'll close enterprise deals in Saudi Arabia's retail and logistics market, and lay the strategic groundwork for Nash's expansion across the region. In both cases, "closing" means more than commercial negotiation. It means understanding a customer's operation deeply enough to design the right solution, working with our product and engineering teams to scope it, and building the business case that makes the investment obvious. Saudi Arabia is one of the most interesting delivery markets in the world right now. Retail and grocery are modernizing fast, quick commerce is scaling nationally, and delivery has moved from an afterthought to core infrastructure. The companies building through this shift need exactly what Nash does. It's a rare combination: real pipeline to close today, a regional expansion thesis to develop alongside it, and direct influence over what Nash builds next. WHAT YOU'LL DO CLOSE NEW ENTERPRISE CUSTOMERS IN KSA Own new enterprise opportunities in the Kingdom end-to-end, from first conversation through to signed partnership. But "sales cycle" undersells what this actually involves. Each deal starts with understanding a customer's delivery operation in detail: how orders flow, which carriers run which zones, where manual workarounds mask systemic problems, what their cost structure actually looks like. From that understanding, you design the Nash solution. Which products apply. How they integrate with existing systems. What the deployment sequence looks like. What outcomes the customer should expect and when. You'll work directly with Nash's product and engineering teams to shape proposals. Sometimes you're configuring what exists. Sometimes you're identifying a gap that becomes a product investment. The best deals at Nash aren't closed by selling features. They're closed by designing a system that solves a problem the customer couldn't solve with their current stack. You'll work with senior operators and executives at retailers, grocery chains, quick commerce companies, and logistics businesses. Nash already works with one of the Kingdom's leading grocery retailers. Your job is to convert that credibility into new partnerships, not by running a volume play, but by identifying the right enterprise accounts and building deep, strategic relationships. In Saudi Arabia, that relationship work is the deal. Trust is built in person, over time, and it compounds. SUPPORT THE GROWTH OF EXISTING STRATEGIC ACCOUNTS Work alongside regional leadership to expand our largest customer relationships. These accounts are multi-product, multi-year partnerships where the next phase of growth depends on identifying what Nash should build and deploy next. This means running structured assessments of a customer's current operations, mapping where new Nash capabilities could change their cost structure or delivery experience, and building the business case that gets a new workstream funded internally. You'll model scenarios: what happens if this retailer shifts 30% of volume from third-party fleets to a captive fleet? What does route optimization save across 150 stores versus 40? What's the real cost of a failed delivery when you account for redelivery, customer churn, and call center load? Some of this work is regulatory as much as commercial. Data residency under PDPL, riyal-denominated commercial structures, and local compliance requirements all shape how solutions get designed and priced in the Kingdom. You don't need to be a lawyer. You need to treat these as design constraints, not obstacles. You'll work closely with Product and Engineering to translate what you learn in the field into product direction. The line between selling and building is thin at Nash. Your customer conversations directly shape our roadmap. This is strategic work, not account management. You're helping senior operators see what's possible and building the commercial and technical structure to get there. LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR GCC EXPANSION Nash's international plan calls for enterprise customers beyond Saudi Arabia. Your job isn't to run a full sales cycle in a new country while also closing deals in the Kingdom. It's to do the strategic groundwork that makes expansion possible: identify which GCC markets have the strongest fit for Nash, map the top 10-20 target accounts, build a view of local carrier ecosystems and competitive dynamics, and start activating warm introduction pathways through Nash's founder network, advisors, and your own connections. This looks like research, relationship-building, and a handful of well-prepared trips rather than sustained in-market selling. You'll build the target list, secure the first executive meetings, and develop enough local context to design a credible entry plan. When a conversation gets serious, you'll work with regional leadership and Nash's global team to shape the engagement. New markets also mean new operational patterns. Delivery in Dubai works differently than delivery in Riyadh, and both work differently than delivery in Sydney or San Francisco. Carrier ecosystems, courier nationalization rules, customer expectations, addressing conventions, and cost structures all shift. Ramadan inverts the demand curve. Summer heat reshapes delivery windows. Cash on delivery still matters in some segments. Part of this work is understanding those differences well enough to know where Nash's existing product translates and where adaptation is needed. BUILD THE PLAYBOOK Every engagement teaches Nash something. You'll capture what works (and what doesn't) across deal cycles, competitive positioning, pricing, and regional nuance. The goal is to leave behind a playbook that makes the next hire faster and the next market easier. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE First 6 months: - Material contribution to multiple new Saudi enterprise deals closed or in final stages - A healthy pipeline of qualified enterprise opportunities with clear next steps - Strategic account value assessments completed, with new use cases scoped and costed - Active collaboration with Product and Engineering on at least one customer-driven product investment - GCC expansion research complete: target market identified, top accounts mapped, initial outreach underway First 12 months: - Material contribution to meaningful new revenue closed from the Saudi enterprise pipeline - A documented, repeatable enterprise sales approach for the Saudi market, including solution design templates and engagement frameworks - First qualified enterprise conversations in a GCC expansion market, with a credible entry plan and timeline - A clear recommendation on where Nash should expand next in the region, what it takes, and when to commit dedicated resources WHO YOU ARE You have 5-10 years of experience, and your career most likely started in management consulting. The profile we expect to hire: formative years at a top-tier strategy firm (McKinsey, Bain, or BCG, or a practice of comparable rigor), followed by a move into an operating, product, or commercial role at a technology, retail, or logistics company. The consulting foundation matters because this role runs on the same muscles: structured problem-solving, executive communication, and building a case rigorous enough to move a board. If you built that toolkit somewhere else, in a strategy seat inside a serious operator, say, make the case. Consulting alone isn't enough, though. Somewhere along the way you've been responsible for commercial outcomes, closing deals, growing accounts, or owning a number, even if your title was never "Account Executive." The common thread: you understand how complex operations work, you can design solutions to hard problems, and you've delivered results, not just recommendations. You think in systems, not features. When you look at a customer's delivery operation, you see the architecture: where data flows, where decisions get made, where the manual workarounds are hiding real cost. You can sketch a solution on a whiteboard in a customer meeting and then translate it into a scoping document for an engineering team the same afternoon. JOB_TITLE: Senior AI Backend Engineer - Agent Evaluation & Quality
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: About the role We run production multi-agent systems that handle real work for a large base of users. As those systems grow, our biggest constraint is confidence: we need to know how well the agents perform, catch regressions before they ship, and keep quality steady as we release. This role owns that. You'll build the evaluation systems behind our agents - the judges, test harnesses, and simulators that tell us whether an agent is working and where it's failing. The goal is to let us ship agents faster because we can trust what the evaluation tells us. Evaluation is the focus, but it won't be the boundary. Because you'll understand the agents' failure modes better than anyone there will also be opportunities to contribute to agent development itself, building and improving the agents alongside the systems that evaluate them. Responsibilities Own the evaluation stack. Design and build LLM-as-judge systems, calibrate them against human labels, and make agent quality measurable per-agent and per-failure-mode. Make the release gate real. Build per-PR eval harnesses and regression detection wired into CI, so quality is enforced automatically, not by manual passes. Build user simulators to generate test coverage and adversarial cases before real users hit them. Turn production signal into improvement - pipe real failures back into evaluation sets so the system compounds over time. Partner with product to turn "what good looks like" into concrete, measurable criteria. Grow into agent development - contribute to building and hardening the agents themselves, starting with the components you know most deeply from evaluating them. Requirements Strong software engineering fundamentals. Production Python or Typescript (or similar), clean API and system design, testing, CI/CD. You write code others build on - evaluation infrastructure is real engineering. Hands-on LLM/agent experience. You've built with LLMs - agents, RAG, tool/function calling, orchestration frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent) - and understand how they behave and break. A measurement mindset. You reason about metrics, calibration, and experiments; you want to quantify whether something works, not just ship it. Production experience. You've run LLM systems in production and dealt with reliability, latency, cost, and observability. 5+ years software engineering, with recent hands-on LLM/agent work. Nice to have Direct experience evaluating LLM/agent systems - offline/online eval, LLM-as-judge, systematic regression testing. Observability tooling (Arize, LangSmith, or similar). Arabic language / NLP experience. E-commerce or merchant-facing product experience.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: We are seeking an experienced and safety-conscious Commissioning & Start-Up (CSU) Lead to oversee the successful transition of our Steam Methane Reformer (SMR) hydrogen production assets from the construction phase to commercial operation. You will lead the field execution team, manage interfaces between engineering, construction, and operations, and ensure that all plant systems are safely commissioned, tested, and fully functional in accordance with project specifications and industry standards. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Strategy: Provide technical and operational leadership for the site commissioning team. Develop and implement the Commissioning Execution Plan, including scheduling, resource mobilization, and budget management. Technical Oversight: Lead the end-to-end commissioning of SMR units, including the reformer furnace, shift converters, PSA (Pressure Swing Adsorption) purification systems, compressors, steam systems, and balance-of-plant (BOP) utilities. Safety & Compliance: Enforce rigorous safety protocols (Permit-to-Work, LOTO, HAZOP/HAZID compliance) throughout the construction, commissioning, and startup phases. Act as a safety champion on-site. Pre-Commissioning & Testing: Manage pre-commissioning activities, including mechanical completion walkdowns, piping system flushing/cleaning, leak testing, instrumentation loop checks, and control system (DCS/PLC) functional validation. Startup & Stabilization: Direct the first-time introduction of feedstocks and gases, manage the ramp-up process, and conduct performance test runs to verify that the plant meets design efficiency and production targets. Documentation & Handover: Ensure all commissioning documentation (test reports, punch lists, as-built records, handover dossiers) is accurate and complete. Facilitate the formal turnover of the facility to the Operations team. Stakeholder Coordination: Act as the primary liaison between project engineering, EPC contractors, vendors/OEMs, and the client/owner’s operations team to resolve technical issues and resolve punch list items efficiently. Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Process Engineering. Experience: Minimum of 10+ years in the oil, gas, or chemical industry, with at least 5 years specifically in a lead capacity for the commissioning and startup of SMR Hydrogen plants . Technical Depth: Deep understanding of SMR process chemistry, thermodynamics, and high-temperature furnace operations. Expertise in hydrogen safety, high-pressure gas systems, and PSA unit operations. Proficiency in interpreting complex P&IDs, control logic, and loop diagrams. Leadership Skills: Proven track record of managing multi-disciplinary site teams and coordinating effectively with contractors and subcontractors. Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills to perform root cause analysis (RCA) during technical troubleshooting of complex process issues. Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills to report progress to stakeholders and train operational personnel on new systems. Preferred Qualifications Experience with other hydrogen technologies (e.g., electrolysis, carbon capture integration). Certification in Project Management (PMP) or relevant industry health and safety certifications. Experience in both greenfield and brownfield project environments. Working Conditions This is a field-based, 100% site-presence role. Must be willing to work at construction sites, which may include remote or international locations. Requires flexibility to work extended hours, weekends, or shifts during critical startup milestones.

JOB_TITLE: Assistant Professor in Water Security and Desalination
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: The Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering (BESE) Division at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is seeking outstanding individuals and change-makers to build ambitious research programs that will push the boundaries of technology and advance the goals of global water security. Among several targeted faculty hires, we are inviting applications from high-caliber candidates for open-rank positions (i.e., Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor) who will bring new insights, tangible solutions and renewed focus to the areas of water security, desalination, and sustainable water systems. The BESE Division welcomes applications from all qualified candidates and particularly encourages applications from Saudi nationals and women in the field. Initial priority areas include, but are not limited to: • Seawater reverse osmosis process optimization • Next-generation membrane and separation technology • Energy-efficient desalination • Brine management, zero-liquid discharge and alternative-source production • Resource recovery and waste valorization • Water system modeling We seek candidates with clear plans for research translation, including collaboration with in-Kingdom and international partners, and a pathway to validate and implement outcomes in real-world contexts. Successful candidates will be expected to establish and sustain a globally visible, externally competitive research program, position KAUST as a global leader in water security, and contribute to graduate teaching, mentoring, and the training of the next generation of scientists and engineers. About KAUST KAUST is a mission-driven graduate research university dedicated to advancing science and technology through interdisciplinary research, education, and innovation. KAUST works closely with national and international partners across academia, industry, and government to translate research into innovative technologies and solutions that support the Kingdom’s strategic priorities, drive economic development, and deliver tangible societal impact. Located on the shores of the Red Sea in Saudi Arabia, KAUST attracts top faculty, scientists, engineers and students from around the world. Faculty benefit from state-of-the-art research facilities, guaranteed baseline research funding, generous infrastructure support, entrepreneurship opportunities, internationally competitive salaries, and a uniquely international campus community designed to enable both professional excellence and family well-being. Ranked #1 in the Arab world in the Times Higher Education Arab University Rankings 2026, KAUST is internationally recognized for its research excellence. Application instructions Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until positions are filled. Successful candidates will be expected to commence their appointments at KAUST in 2027. Interested applicants should submit the following materials: • A cover letter, including the rank sought and alignment with the priority area(s) • A 2-3 page curriculum vitae, including links to your Google Scholar and Scopus profiles • A 2-3 page research statement describing a 5-year vision and startup plan • A 2-page teaching and mentoring statement • A one-paragraph summary of each of your top five publications, describing your contribution, the novelty of the work, and its impact • Contact information for 3-5 referees who are acknowledged experts in the field from academia, industry, or other relevant sectors Recruitment is conducted in accordance with KAUST hiring practices and will emphasize transparent, equitable, and internationally benchmarked evaluation.

Talk to users, read the data, and work out what is actually broken - Size the problem honestly and say what you would not do Design - Design the solution in Figma: flows, screens, states, edge cases - Take the work through critique with the product and design team and rework it - Hand off to engineers and stay with the build through release After launch - Measure what happened and say plainly whether it worked - Bring the result back to the team, including when the answer is no Working across teams - Work with engineers, analysts and product managers on the same problem - Present your work, defend the decisions, and change your mind when the evidence says so - Write clearly enough that someone who was not in the room can act on it Skills, Knowledge & Expertise - 18 or over - Evidence that you can make a product decision, not just draw a screen. Both are judged the same way and no translation is needed - Willingness to have your work argued with, and to argue back with evidence - Any shipped work: a personal app, a university project that reached real users, freelance product work - Basic comfort with data: reading a funnel, understanding what a metric is actually saying - Front-end familiarity, enough to know what is cheap and what is expensive to build - Interest in fintech, payments, or how people in Saudi actually handle money - Professional product or design experience - A degree in design - A polished portfolio. Work in progress counts - Certifications of any kind Egilibility, Format and Dates - Anyone living in Saudi Arabia, 18 or over, citizens and residents alike, entering as individuals - There are no team entries - Current Tabby employees and contractors, their immediate families, and anyone who left Tabby in the last twelve months cannot enter - We expect a full-time level of engagement. The internship is not part-time. Performance, ownership and involvement are expected at a full-time level - Six months, starting after the final in mid-October 2026 - Funded and paid in full by Tabby, SAR 3,000 a month - Full integration into a product or design team at Tabby, matched to the work you did in the challenge - Distributed team across multiple countries. If you are based in Riyadh, the working mode is office-first - A path to a junior role on the team afterwards. That is our intent and what we aim for, not a guarantee: it depends on how the internship goes - Three places are open, first, second and third, and each one is this role - Subject to a separate contract and the required eligibility checks - 16 September, entries open - 30 September, entries close - 15 October, the final, where you present live. It replaces the interview Enter at tabby.sa/en-SA/engineering/imagine. The same page in Arabic is at tabby.sa/ar-SA/engineering/imagine. This internship is intentionally demanding and designed for people aiming for fast professional growth in product and design.
