A Logistics Operations Supervisor plays a crucial role in overseeing the movement of goods and ensuring efficient supply chain management. Below are the key job responsibilities of a Logistics Operations Supervisor: 1. Oversee and manage logistics staff, including warehouse, coordinators, and support personnel. Provide leadership, assign tasks, monitor performance, and foster a positive and productive team environment. 2. Train new and existing staff on company policies, safety procedures, and logistics operations. Conduct periodic training sessions and ensure team members are well-informed of any updates or changes to processes. 3. Develop and maintain employee schedules, ensuring proper staffing levels to meet operational demands. Address staffing issues such as absenteeism, overtime, and shift coverage. 4. Monitor and manage the day-to-day activities of the logistics operations, including co-ordination with suppliers for shipments, receiving, storing, and shipping goods, inventory management, and order fulfillment. 5. Analyze the efficiency of the logistics processes, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to streamline operations, reduce turnaround time, and increase productivity. 6. Ensure that the goods being handled are accurate, damage-free, and meet quality standards. Enforce strict checks on inventory and shipments to ensure high-quality standards are maintained. 7. Maintain up-to-date records of inventory levels and movements. Monitor stock levels, reorder points, and perform regular stock checks to avoid overstocking or stockouts. 8. Ensure that stock rotation principles (FIFO, FEFO, etc.) are followed to reduce spoilage, waste, or obsolescence, especially for perishable or time-sensitive goods. 9. Perform regular physical inventories and reconcile discrepancies between the system and actual stock levels. Investigate and resolve inventory issues such as misplaced, lost, or damaged goods. 10. Coordinate and schedule inbound and outbound shipments, customer requirements, and delivery deadlines. Ensure timely dispatch of goods and track shipments to avoid delays. 11. Liaise with third-party logistics providers (3PL), shipping carriers, and freight forwarders to arrange transportation. Negotiate rates, establish contracts, and ensure the best carrier options are chosen for cost and time efficiency. 12. Plan the most efficient routes for transportation to minimize costs and ensure timely deliveries. 13. Continuously assess and evaluate logistics processes to identify inefficiencies, redundancies, and areas for improvement. Implement new systems or workflows to enhance productivity and reduce costs. 14. Identify and implement strategies to reduce logistics-related costs, such as reducing transportation expenses, improving packaging methods, or negotiating better rates with suppliers and carriers. 15. Track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to logistics efficiency (e.g., on-time delivery, transportation costs, inventory turnover, etc.) and ensure the team meets or exceeds targets. 16. Ensure logistics operations comply with local regulations regarding transportation, storage, handling of goods, and employee safety. 17. Enforce safety policies and guidelines, including proper handling of hazardous materials, safe lifting techniques, vehicle safety, and emergency response protocols. Ensure that all staff are trained in these safety procedures. 18. Conduct risk assessments to identify potential hazards in the logistics operations and develop mitigation strategies to prevent accidents or delays. 19. Communicate with internal and external customers regarding delivery schedules, status updates, and any issues related to logistics. Ensure that customer complaints are handled quickly and effectively. 20. Ensure that all customer orders are processed accurately, efficiently, and delivered on time. Work with the sales and support service teams to resolve any order fulfillment issues. 21. Investigate and resolve any logistical issues, including delayed shipments, inventory discrepancies, damaged goods, or transport accidents. Act swiftly to mitigate the impact on customers and business operations. 22. Ensure that all required documentation, such as bills of lading, shipping manifests, inventory records, and regulatory forms, is accurate and filed in a timely manner. 23. Utilizing inhouse system for full business flow cycle (shipping documents / Cargo Insurance - SRV's - DN's – credit note, etc. 24. Develop and maintain positive relationships with suppliers and service providers, ensuring effective collaboration and addressing any supply chain disruptions. In summary, a Logistics Operations Supervisor is responsible for ensuring the smooth operation of all logistics processes, from managing teams to optimizing inventory levels, coordinating transportation, and continuously improving efficiency. They play a critical role in maintaining cost-effective, timely, and safe logistics practices while ensuring customer satisfaction.

The Senior Director, Event Mobility Planning is accountable for establishing and leading the integrated mobility planning capability for major events, festivals, sporting competitions and entertainment activations across the city program. The role ensures the safe, efficient and coordinated movement of guests, athletes, performers, VIPs, workforce, volunteers, logistics vehicles, emergency services and public transport users across venues, districts and transport modes. The position acts as the City Operations mobility lead and coordination authority for major events. Strategy, Governance and Function Leadership · Develop, maintain and implement the Programme Event Mobility Strategy, governance framework, operating model, standards, policies and planning calendar. · Create a scalable mobility capability covering business-as-usual destination operations, recurring events, overlapping event programmes and major-event overlays. · Define clear accountabilities, decision rights, escalation routes and interfaces across City Operations, districts, venues, transport operators, security, emergency services and government stakeholders. · Lead the permanent mobility planning team and mobilise specialist consultants, service providers and temporary event resources as required. · Provide executive advice, decision papers, options, risk assessments, cost implications and recommendations on event mobility matters. 2. Integrated Event Mobility Planning · Lead the development, assurance and approval of integrated Event Mobility Plans for the full event lifecycle, from concept and feasibility through readiness, live delivery and post-event review. · Convert event attendance profiles, venue capacities, session schedules and origin-destination assumptions into transport demand forecasts, mode-share targets and time-phased arrival and departure plans. · Plan distinct mobility journeys for general admission guests, hospitality customers, VIPs, athletes, performers, officials, workforce, volunteers, media, people of determination and emergency responders. · Coordinate mobility plans across simultaneous events to manage cumulative demand, shared infrastructure, operational conflicts and network resilience. · Maintain an integrated mobility planning schedule with defined submissions, reviews, approvals, exercises and operational handover gates. 3. Traffic, Access and Parking Planning · Oversee Traffic Management Plans, road network assessments, access-control strategies, temporary traffic management, diversions, closures, pick-up and drop-off areas and emergency access routes. · Develop event parking strategies covering pre-booked parking, park-and-ride, VIP and hospitality allocation, workforce parking, accessible parking, overflow arrangements and parking technology. · Ensure vehicle access, accreditation and permit arrangements align with security zoning, venue ingress and egress, logistics windows and public-realm requirements. · Use modelling, scenario testing and live operational data to validate assumptions and optimise road, kerbside and parking capacity. 4. Public Transport, Shuttle and Active Mobility Integration · Design integrated bus, shuttle, public transport, taxi and ride-hailing service plans with clear capacities, frequencies, staging, layover, dispatch, queuing and passenger information requirements. · Coordinate park-and-ride and remote transport hub operations, including fleet sizing, boarding processes, accessibility, contingency vehicles and demand management. · Integrate walking, micromobility and last-mile routes with venue, public-realm, wayfinding, crowd management and accessibility plans. · Agree service levels, operational interfaces and recovery arrangements with mobility operators and delivery partners. 5. VIP, Hospitality and Specialist Movements · Develop secure, discreet and service-led mobility plans for Royal, government, VIP, sponsor, hospitality and protocol movements. · Coordinate premium ground transport, coach, chauffeur, charter and aviation interfaces where required, in partnership with security, protocol and specialist providers. · Establish holding, dispatch, route, access, parking and contingency arrangements that protect both guest experience and network performance. 6. Logistics and Operational Interface · Integrate freight, servicing, waste, catering, retail, broadcast and contractor movements with the guest mobility plan to minimise conflicts and maintain operational continuity. · Coordinate delivery routes, vehicle staging, holding areas, time windows, access permits and back-of-house interfaces with the City Logistics function and venue operators. · Ensure emergency service routes and incident response access are protected throughout build, event and breakdown phases. 7. Operational Readiness and Live Event Delivery · Lead mobility readiness reviews, tabletop exercises, simulations, test events, route proving and operational rehearsals. · Define mobility command, control, communications, reporting and escalation arrangements, including integration with the City Command and Control Unit and relevant event control rooms. · Provide senior mobility leadership during live operations, ensuring timely decisions, coordinated issue resolution and deployment of contingency measures. · Lead structured post-event reviews, capture lessons learned and ensure corrective actions are incorporated into future plans and standards. 8. Stakeholder, Commercial and Supplier Management · Build effective working relationships with transport authorities, traffic police, emergency services, public transport operators, districts, venues, hotels, event organisers, service providers and relevant government entities. · Lead multi-agency mobility workshops, design reviews, readiness forums and executive reporting. · Develop scopes, procurement strategies and performance requirements for mobility planning, modelling, technology and event delivery services. · Ensure suppliers are appropriately qualified, locally compliant and capable of mobilising suitable Saudi-based resources and workforce development plans. · Own assigned budgets, forecasts, commercial evaluations, contract performance and value-for-money initiatives. Requirements Education · Bachelor's degree in Transport Planning, Civil or Transportation Engineering, Urban Planning, Logistics, Operations Management or a related discipline. · Master's degree in a relevant discipline is preferred. · Professional membership or certification in transport planning, traffic engineering, project management, event management or a related field is desirable. Experience · Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in transport planning, mobility operations, traffic engineering, major event transport (FIFA World Cup or Olympics), city operations or major infrastructure, including at least 8 years in senior leadership roles. · Demonstrable accountability for mobility planning and operational delivery for major sporting, entertainment, cultural or destination events. · Proven experience leading multidisciplinary teams and coordinating multiple transport modes, agencies, venues and service providers in complex operating environments. · Experience developing transport demand forecasts, event mobility plans, traffic management plans, parking strategies, public transport services and operational readiness programmes. · Strong commercial experience covering procurement, consultant and operator management, budget control, service levels and performance management. · Experience in Saudi Arabia, the GCC, major destination developments or giga-project environments is strongly preferred. Preferred Background · Leadership experience supporting Formula One, international football, Olympic or Asian Games, major tennis, large festivals, concerts, exhibitions or comparable high-attendance events. · Experience within a city authority, transport authority, integrated resort, major destination, venue cluster, event organising committee or transport consultancy/operator. · Practical exposure to transport command and control, intelligent transport systems, mobility technology, crowd integration, accessibility and sustainability programmes. Technical & Functional Expectations · Transport demand forecasting, mode-share planning, network and junction modelling, scenario testing and data-led decision-making. · Event mobility planning, traffic management, public transport and shuttle planning, parking, kerbside, taxi and ride-hailing operations. · Guest, workforce, VIP, logistics, emergency service, accessibility and last-mile journey planning. · Operational readiness, exercising, command and control, incident management, contingency planning and post-event assurance. · Commercial strategy, scope development, tender evaluation, contract management, budget forecasting and supplier performance. · Executive governance, stakeholder negotiation, written reporting, risk management and cross-functional coordination.

At Salla, we are building the digital backbone of commerce in the region, empowering thousands of merchants to start, grow, and scale their businesses. We turn what's complex into something simple, powerful, and scalable. Catalog is the layer underneath everything. Storefronts, search, recommendations, landing pages, and every channel a merchant sells through all read from the same product data. When it is good, every surface above it gets better at once. When it is thin or wrong, nothing built on top can fix it. Two things make this exciting:. First, Salla does not build the catalog. Merchants do, and often not even the merchant: a freelancer, operations staff, an outsourced agency. Every surface we build inherits what those hands produce. So the question is not how to clean the data. It is how you change what someone produces when they do not work for you and mostly want to finish and move on. Second, no two categories need the same product record. What a fashion merchant needs is not what a pharmacy, a grocer, or a gold merchant needs. The easy answer is to build each category separately, and it does not scale. You will drive impact across five areas The Catalog Engine and Category Setup (one engine, built once, with what each category needs from a product record expressed as configuration rather than code, so supporting one more category is fast and repeatable) Product Data Input (creation, bulk import, editing, and everything that happens at the moment someone types or uploads) Structure and Meaning (taxonomy, attributes, variants, identifiers, normalization, and duplicates) AI Enrichment (extracting and generating product data from what merchants already have, with a clear position on confidence, review, and correction) Downstream Fitness (how this data actually performs where it is consumed: search results, storefronts, recommendations, and external channel feeds) Responsibilities: Own the catalog strategy end to end: sequence it into quarters, defend it in the room, and hold it accountable to the numbers it promised. Own the roadmap for how product data gets created and improved on Salla, prioritized on whether the data works downstream rather than on how many fields are filled. Design for the people who actually do the work, including the ones who do not own the store, and make the good path the fastest path rather than a longer one enforced by rules. Keep a new category, a configuration change rather than an engineering project, and be able to show the difference in effort between the first one and the next. Put AI to work where it earns trust: decide what we generate outright, what we suggest for approval, and what we never touch, with a stated confidence policy and a loop that learns from every correction a merchant makes. Define what catalog quality means at Salla and instrument it honestly, tied to the surfaces that consume the data rather than to completeness for its own sake. Own how product data performs in external selling channels, where the requirements are strict and the rejections are visible. Decide how much structure we impose and where merchants stay free, then defend that line against pressure from both directions. Lead 2 to 3 product managers: give them real ownership, coach their framing and craft, run a reliable cadence, and raise the quality bar of what the group ships. Work as one system with the teams that depend on this data: search and discovery, storefronts, vendors, marketplace, and data. Requirements Six or more years in product management, including work on a self-serve platform where users created their own content or data and you were accountable for the quality of what they produced. A number you owned and moved on that data: completeness that meant something, accuracy, time to publish, adoption of a data tool, or the performance of that data somewhere downstream. Evidence that you changed what users produced at the moment they produced it, rather than cleaning it up afterwards in a pipeline. We will ask which one it was. Platform judgment: you have built something once and made it serve many cases through configuration, and you can explain where you drew the line between what was shared and what was specific, and what that choice cost you. AI in production for structured data: extraction, classification, generation, or matching. You can talk concretely about confidence thresholds, error rates, what you let through automatically, and what you did when it was wrong at scale. Literacy in how product data is actually structured: taxonomies, attribute schemas, variants, identifiers, matching and deduplication, and the strict requirements external selling channels impose. You have coached product managers, formally or not, and you are ready to lead a small team without stepping away from the craft yourself. You own outcomes rather than roadmaps, you move quickly through ambiguity, and you build clarity where others see noise. You stay close to the details and you cannot guard your own area, because this data belongs to everyone downstream. Full professional fluency in Arabic and English is required. Merchant context in this region is preferred over theoretical knowledge. Willing to relocate to Saudi Arabia and work on-site.

ABOUT TAKEIN TakeIn is a food delivery platform on a mission to make food delivery fairer — for customers and for restaurants. We launched in January 2025 in the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia and are live in production, processing real orders daily. We're hiring across product, engineering, and operations to scale what we've built. The Opportunity We're a newly launched, ambitious food delivery startup in Dammam, and we're looking for a product manager to join the product team. The best part: you'll see the impact of your work every week. We're adding users every day and we watch our metrics closely. You'll get to work across every part of a B2C mobile product, in the age of AI. We enjoy what we are building, we enjoy being a team, and we believe we're building something huge. Your Day-to-Day - Learn the Point of Sale app properly in your first few weeks. Not a demo walkthrough; you'll need to know how a restaurant actually uses it before you change anything, and how the whole food delivery system fits together around it. You won't be alone: the team is here to support you. - Own one product end to end: take the direction you're given, write the PRD, refine it with the dev team, get stakeholders aligned, and drive it until it's live. Then measure the outcome. - Unblock the operations team. Most of what you pick up first is POS work that is actively slowing down restaurant onboarding. - Grow into the admin dashboard and the customer app as your scope widens. - Talk to the people who use what you build: customers, restaurant owners, and our own ops team in Saudi. - Work directly with design and engineering. Small team, short lines, nothing to route around. - Ship weekly and look at what happened. You'll see the result of your decisions in days, not quarters. What You Bring - At least 3 years as a product manager or product owner, most of it in a startup or a small, fast-moving team. If your career has been one narrow slice of a large corporate product, this will not feel like the same job. - B2C mobile product experience, shipped, with real users. This one isn't flexible. - Experience with internal tools, dashboards, or ops products. - You write clear PRDs, research them deeply, and get them approved without a month of meetings. - Comfortable with data. Whatever tool you used, you can define the metric, pull the number, and change your mind when it tells you something you didn't expect. - Arabic and English at a working level. Arabic for the Saudi market and our ops team, English for the product and engineering team. - You understand the Saudi market, or you've built for it. You don't have to live there. - You use AI in your actual workflow, not as a talking point. Be ready to say what got faster for you in the last two years, and how. - You follow product seriously. The books, the podcasts, the people you learn from. We will ask. Bonus - Food delivery, q-commerce, or e-commerce experience. - You've worked on a POS, restaurant tech, or a logistics product before. - Figma, enough to work inside a file rather than only comment on it. - Jira, Linear, Mixpanel, Metabase, or whatever you used instead. - Marketing experience. - You've launched something into Saudi or the wider GCC. - A degree in computer science or engineering. How We Work - The products: customer app, POS, driver app, admin dashboard. - The team: product, design, mobile, backend, and operations; all one Slack message away. - Your manager: the product lead, who sets the direction and hands you well-defined problems. This is an execution-heavy role by design. You won't be staring at a blank page, and if that's what you're looking for, this isn't it. We use an AI notetaker during interviews to help us stay focused on the conversation. You'll be asked for consent before any recording begins. If you need accommodations at any point in the process, let us know in your application.

The Safety Specialist will support the Safety Lead in implementing and maintaining occupational health and safety programs across KAUST facilities, operations, maintenance activities, construction works, and projects . The role will focus on field inspections, audits, risk assessments, incident investigations, safety documentation, contractor engagement, training, corrective action tracking, and compliance with ISO 45001, HSE policies, and applicable regulatory requirements . The position requires a strong field-oriented HSE professional who can identify hazards, evaluate risks, provide practical safety guidance, investigate incidents, and work effectively with facility owners, project teams, contractors, and service providers. Key Responsibilities HSE Program Implementation: Support the Safety Lead in implementing and continuously improving risk-based safety programs across facilities, operations, maintenance, construction, and projects. Safety Inspections & Audits: Conduct risk-based site inspections, safety audits, compliance evaluations, and field verifications to ensure HSE requirements are being followed. Risk Assessment: Perform hazard identification and risk assessments and verify that appropriate control measures are implemented and effective. Safety Documentation Review: Review HSE documents including risk assessments, method statements, safety plans, permits-to-work, lifting plans, excavation plans, confined-space controls, electrical work procedures, and MOC documentation. Incident Investigation: Investigate or support investigations of accidents, injuries, incidents, and near misses, identify root causes, and recommend corrective and preventive actions. Corrective Action Tracking: Monitor corrective and preventive actions arising from inspections, audits, investigations, and observations, ensuring timely closure and escalation of overdue actions. HSE Training & Awareness: Develop and deliver safety training, toolbox talks, workshops, permit-to-work training, and awareness programs to improve employee and contractor competency. Stakeholder & Contractor Support: Provide practical HSE guidance to facility owners, project teams, contractors, service providers, and other stakeholders to support safe execution of activities. HSE Reporting & Data Analysis: Collect and analyze HSE data, KPIs, inspection findings, audit results, incident trends, and corrective action status, providing reports and recommendations to management. Safety Culture & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture, intervene in unsafe activities, communicate lessons learned, maintain accurate HSE records, and support compliance with ISO 45001, regulations, policies, procedures, and industry best practices. Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Engineering, Science, or a related safety discipline is required. Professional Certification: ISO 45001 Lead Auditor certification is required. Incident Investigation: Certification or formal training in Incident Root Cause Analysis is required. HSE Experience: Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in occupational safety, facilities safety, construction safety, contractor management, projects, auditing, compliance, or related HSE functions. Risk Management: Strong experience in hazard identification, risk assessment, risk control, and implementation of risk-based safety programs. High-Risk Activities: Practical knowledge of safety controls for work at height, lifting operations, excavation, confined spaces, hot work, electrical work, and permit-to-work systems. ISO & Audit Knowledge: Working knowledge of ISO 45001, safety management systems, auditing, inspections, incident investigation, and corrective action management. Knowledge of ISO 19011 and ISO 31000 is an advantage. Safety Certifications: Additional recognized HSE qualifications such as CSP, CHST, NEBOSH Certificate/Diploma, IOSH, or equivalent are preferred. Train-the-Trainer certification is also an advantage. Communication & Reporting: Excellent English communication skills with the ability to prepare professional HSE reports, inspection records, investigation reports, presentations, and safety documentation.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: About Agoda At Agoda, we bridge the world through travel. Our story began in 2005, when two lifelong friends and entrepreneurs, driven by their passion for travel, launched Agoda to make it easier for everyone to explore the world. Today, we are part of Booking Holdings [NASDAQ: BKNG], with a diverse team of over 7,000 people from 90 countries, working together in offices around the globe. If you’re ready to begin your best journey and help build travel for the world, join us. Get To Know Our Team: The Data department oversees all of Agoda’s data-related requirements. Our ultimate goal is to enable and increase the use of data in the company through creative approaches and the implementation of powerful resources such as operational and analytical databases, queue systems, BI tools, and data science technology. We hire the brightest minds from around the world to take on this challenge and equip them with the knowledge and tools that contribute to their personal growth and success while supporting our company’s culture of diversity and experimentation. The role the Data team plays at Agoda is critical as business users, product managers, engineers, and many others rely on us to empower their decision making. We are equally dedicated to our customers by improving their search experience with faster results and protecting them from any fraudulent activities. Data is interesting only when you have enough of it, and we have plenty. This is what drives up the challenge as part of the Data department, but also the reward. The Opportunity: As a Senior/Staff Data Engineer in CEG (Customer Experience Group), you will help design, build, and maintain the data and software foundations that power how CEG Business users serves customers and agents across all contact channels. You will work closely with Product, Operations, Analytics, Operations Efficiency, WFM, DevOps and engineering teams to deliver reliable data pipelines, scalable models, internal tools, and clear insights that improve customer experience and operational efficiency. You can talk to both engineers and business stakeholders in simple, clear language. At the Staff level, you will also shape CEG’s data and tooling strategy, influence cross‑team architecture, and raise the overall engineering and data bar for the team. What You’ll Do: Data Engineering - Design, build, and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest, transform, and serve data from CEG systems (case management, telephony, chat, bots, QA tools, WFM, CRM) and third‑party tools and logs. - Develop and optimize data models (e.g., warehouse tables, marts, views) that power CEG reporting, monitoring, forecasting, QA, and experimentation. - Ensure data quality, reliability, and observability: - Implement validation checks, anomaly detection, and monitoring for key CEG datasets and metrics. - Work with stakeholders to define and enforce data definitions, SLAs, and ownership for critical tables and metrics. - Improve performance and cost efficiency of data jobs and queries (e.g., partitioning, indexing, query tuning, storage format optimization) for high‑volume CEG data (calls, chats, emails, cases, events). - Collaborate with data platform and engineering teams to standardize tooling and best practices (e.g., version control, CI/CD for data and services, code review, documentation, runbooks). Data Tools & Product Development - Design and build data tools and internal products for CEG (e.g., self‑service analytics, case monitoring dashboards, alerting systems, investigator tools, QA/review tools, agent performance views). - Use languages such as Python, Java, Golang, or JavaScript/TypeScript to implement APIs, data services, and lightweight UIs that expose data in a usable way to agents, managers, and operations teams. - Work closely with CEG product managers and operations to translate operational pain points into concrete data tools, from problem framing to delivery and iteration. - Apply solid software engineering practices—testing, code reviews, CI/CD, observability—to data products so they are reliable, maintainable, and easy to extend. - At Staff level, define and drive the roadmap for key CEG data tools and platforms, ensuring reuse across regions, lines of business, and channels. Data Analytics & Business Impact - Partner with CEG product and business teams to translate questions into data problems and design clear analytic approaches. - Build and maintain dashboards and reports (e.g., contact volumes, handling time, quality, customer outcomes, agent performance, spot alerts) that provide reliable metrics and self‑service access to data. - Perform deep‑dive analysis to understand trends in contact patterns, customer issues, agent performance, and operational efficiency; identify root causes and propose practical, data‑driven recommendations. - Define and maintain metrics and KPIs (e.g., CSAT, NPS, SLA, AHT, FCR, quality scores), ensuring consistent definitions across CEG teams and tools. - Communicate findings in simple, business‑friendly language, including clear implications and recommended next steps. Stakeholder & Team Collaboration - - Act as a trusted data partner for CEG stakeholders (operations leaders, product managers, WFM, QA, training, policy, and regional leadership). - Work with other data engineers, analysts, and scientists to align on data standards, reusable components, and shared datasets for CEG. - Mentor junior and mid‑level team members on data engineering, analytics, and software engineering best practices. - Contribute to continuous improvement of team workflows (code reviews, testing, documentation, runbooks, knowledge sharing, incident reviews). - At Staff level, influence cross‑team architecture and ways of working, making sure CEG’s data ecosystem scales with business growth. The role sits within a high-security family environment and demands absolute discretion. Only clinicians of the highest calibre and professional composure are considered. The Mandate • Confidential residential nursing care within a Royal Household. • Practice within a high-security, high-fidelity family environment. • Absolute discretion as a standing condition. • A permanent engagement with long-term contract stability. Candidate Requirements • Registered Nurse with current licensure. • Minimum five years private duty or residential care experience. • Trained and licensed in a Tier-1 UK or European system — UK, Ireland, or an accepted European jurisdiction. • Fluent English essential; strict NDA compliance mandatory. Package • £58,000 – £68,000 per annum, tax-free. • Private on-compound accommodation and full relocation support. • Comprehensive medical insurance, annual flights home, long-term contract stability. • SCFHS licensing and documentation support guided at every step — see Gulf Healthcare Licensing Support. What this appointment asks of you The appointment is residential nursing inside a high-security Royal Household, and its character is defined by two things: permanence and discretion. You will provide continuous nursing for named members of the family — routine health management, medication governance, wound and post-procedural care when needed, escalation to the household physician — and you will do it as a fixture of the household rather than a visiting professional. The environment is calm, well-resourced and closely protected; protocol matters, punctuality matters, and the ability to be clinically authoritative without ever being conspicuous matters most of all. Nurses with private duty or residential experience will find the pace measured and the standards exacting. Licensing sequence: SCFHS, Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabia licenses clinicians through the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties (SCFHS) on the Mumaris Plus platform. For a residential appointment the sequence runs as follows: • DataFlow primary source verification of your nursing degree, current registration (NMC, NMBI or your European regulator), certificate of good standing and experience letters on institutional letterhead — typically four to eight weeks when the dossier is complete on submission. • SCFHS professional classification, which sets your title and grade; SCFHS may require its nursing licensing examination for some classifications — we confirm your exemption status before you commit to anything. • Professional registration and licence issuance, followed by the work visa, the medical fitness examination and the iqama (residency permit) on arrival. • Household onboarding: NDA execution, accommodation, banking and the practical steps we coordinate with the family office before your first day. With a complete dossier on day one we usually see SCFHS eligibility inside ten to fourteen weeks; the visa and residency stage then runs in parallel with relocation planning. Our notes on SCFHS and Mumaris Plus in 2026 and on the DataFlow workflow set out what to prepare, and good-standing certificates explains the one document that most often delays a file. European-registered nurses should also read the SCFHS pathway for European nursing registrations. How the package is structured The figure quoted above — £58,000 – £68,000 per annum — is base remuneration, and it is paid tax-free: Saudi Arabia levies no personal income tax on employment earnings, so the number on the offer is the number that arrives. Accommodation, flights and medical cover are provided in addition to base, which is what makes the net position so different from a UK or European salary: with housing and travel carried by the household, most of the base figure is savings capacity. Health insurance in Gulf contracts explains the cover clauses worth reading twice. End-of-service gratuity accrues under local labour law for each completed year and is paid when the contract ends; our note on end-of-service gratuity and repatriation explains how it is calculated and what to check in the contract. If you are leaving the UK part-way through a tax year, split-year treatment under the Statutory Residence Test usually applies; keep a day-count from the date you leave and take advice from a cross-border adviser — we point every candidate to one, and tax-free wealth preservation for Gulf clinicians sets out the planning points. Run your own comparison with the UK versus GCC net position calculator or the Gulf net package estimator; we are happy to walk through the result with you before any interview. Living in Riyadh Riyadh is the Kingdom’s capital and its administrative centre, and the city has changed at a pace that surprises clinicians who last visited a decade ago: new districts, a metro, an events calendar that runs through the winter, and a residential market that ranges from the Diplomatic Quarter to the established international compounds in the north of the city. Household appointments normally come with accommodation on the estate or in a compound chosen by the family, so your decision is about days off rather than house-hunting. Winters are mild and bright; summers are hot and lived indoors or early in the day. London is around seven hours by direct flight. Families relocating with children have a wide choice of British and American curriculum schools — our international school fees benchmark sets out fees — and the Riyadh districts and compounds guide covers districts, compounds and commuting; the cultural adjustment guide covers the unwritten rules. How the search is run We run this search as a full-cycle search under a retained, confidential mandate. The first conversation is with Vanessa, our Executive Search Lead, and it is a briefing rather than a screening: what the appointment involves day to day, what the household selects for, and whether it fits the life you want. Your CV goes nowhere until you say so. If you proceed, your dossier is checked against the licensing route above, the household is briefed on an anonymised profile, and interviews run by video before an in-person meeting arranged by the family. Offer, NDA and contract are settled before any licensing fee is incurred. The Staff Manufacturing Test Engineer – Powertrain will serve as a senior technical leader responsible for defining, integrating, and sustaining manufacturing test strategies across Lucid’s electric powertrain systems, including traction inverters, Drive Units, and high‑voltage battery assemblies. This role is focused on systems-level test ownership, ensuring alignment of test architecture, data strategy, safety standards, and validation methodology across powertrain commodities—while partnering closely with commodity‑level test engineers, Design Engineering, Controls, Quality, Production, and external equipment suppliers. As a Staff‑level engineer, this role emphasizes technical authority, cross‑functional leadership, and strategic scalability, rather than day‑to‑day ownership of individual test stations. You Will Serve as the manufacturing test technical authority for powertrain systems, providing oversight and direction across inverter, Drive Unit, and battery test architectures. Review and approve powertrain‑level test strategies, specifications, and major change requests from Design Engineering, ensuring consistency, manufacturability, and scalability across commodities. Define common test principles for end‑of‑line (EOL) and in‑process testing, including test sequencing philosophy, limit strategies, failure‑mode handling, safety requirements, and data traceability. Act as a key escalation point for complex production issues, supporting root‑cause analysis, yield improvement, and false‑fail reduction across powertrain test operations. Collaborate with factory data and analytics teams to enable consistent test data architecture, serial‑level traceability, yield dashboards, and long‑term quality monitoring across powertrain systems. Support training strategies for operations and maintenance teams, ensuring safe operation and effective troubleshooting of high‑voltage powertrain test systems. You Bring Bachelor’s Degree in Controls Systems Engineering, Electrical and Controls Engineering, or Automation and Control Engineering and at least 5 years of professional experience. 8+ years of experience developing, launching, and supporting automated test equipment in high‑volume manufacturing environments. Prior experience with EV powertrain systems, with direct exposure to two or more of the following areas: traction inverters, electric motors / Drive Units, or high‑voltage battery modules or packs. Strong understanding of high‑voltage EV systems, including safety requirements, insulation resistance, hipot testing, functional power testing, and energy storage hazards. Proven ability to define test strategies without being limited to hands‑on station ownership across all commodities simultaneously. Experience guiding test hardware design using platforms such as National Instruments PXI, cDAQ, or cRIO, or equivalent industrial test architectures. Strong software development or technical review experience with tools such as NI LabVIEW, NI TestStand, Python, MATLAB, Vector / CANoe, or similar manufacturing test frameworks. Working knowledge of automotive communication protocols, including CAN, CAN‑FD, LIN, and Automotive Ethernet. Proficiency reviewing electrical schematics and system layouts using tools such as AutoCAD or EPLAN. Experience interfacing test systems with PLCs and industrial networks such as Ethernet/IP or OPC‑UA. Demonstrated ability to lead cross‑functional technical discussions, influence design decisions, and provide clear direction across engineering, production, quality, and suppliers. Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to balance strategic oversight and hands‑on technical problem solving when required. We're looking for a Tech Principal to lead technical strategy and execution on our most ambitious product work: lighthouse projects inside Thoughtworks' global Customer Experience, Product and Design team. Here's the shape of it. A client arrives with a big idea and not much time. Within a few days, you've helped them turn it into a concept everyone agrees on. Within a few weeks, there's something real that customers can actually use and react to. Within a quarter, it's live. Then you do it again, somewhere else in the world, with a different team, and you leave both of them better at it than they were before. If you have built a career integrating strategy, architecture, AI engineering, and executive collaboration, this role offers an ideal platform to leverage those skills. The approach you'd be leading: We call it 3/3/3 3 days: Product concept. Everyone aligned on scope, objectives and how we'll measure success. 3 weeks: Working prototype. Desirability, viability and feasibility tested with real users. 3 months: MLP launch. A production-grade minimum lovable product, ready to keep evolving. Think of it as a reference tempo rather than a fixed schedule. The sequence is what we believe in: align quickly, get real evidence early, put something usable in front of customers while the idea is still current. A regulated platform with a heavy integration surface won't run like a greenfield mobile app, and reading the difference is part of the job. AI runs through all of it, and not as a feature we add at the end. We use AI across the whole lifecycle, from specification and design through build, test and operations, and you'd be one of the people defining what good looks like there. Who You'd Work With We work in tight forward-deployed pods: one Product Strategist, one Experience Designer, and two Forward-Deployed Engineers. You're one of the FDEs — the lead engineer on the pod — guiding architecture, delivery cadence, and technical commercial choices, while collaborating with the strategist and designer as equal partners rather than a downstream requirements queue. Some of the best moments in this job happen when team members explore a challenge from complementary perspectives and unlock innovative solutions. On larger programmes you'll lead across multiple pods, each running its own 3/3/3 rhythm — sometimes a mix of Product Innovation, Modernization/Engineering and Data & AI pod types depending on the engagement shape. You'd report to Ahmet Sakar, Director of Technology for CXPD, and operate as part of a small Tech Principal cadre collaborating directly as peers. Lighthouse projects come in all sizes. Sometimes it's one pod and a single product bet. Sometimes it's a multi-year programme with several streams running at once, real platform and modernization work underneath, and a steering committee to keep alongside. Either way, the work is visible, and when it lands it becomes the case study, the reference architecture and the talk you get invited to give. How Autonomous You Are This is a Tech Principal role, not a Tech Lead. Within Thoughtworks' Radar and CXPD's delivery standards, you make the calls: architecture patterns, stack selection, pod composition for your engagements, commercial pricing tolerances within the band, and the technical position in a pitch. Ahmet is the escalation point for the largest bets, cross-region consistency questions, and firm-wide precedent — everything else lands with you. This isn't a role where every decision gets a second look before it lands with the client. Working in KSA This role anchors in Riyadh, working across the Kingdom's most ambitious digital bets — Vision 2030-aligned government transformation, PIF-family portfolio companies, financial services, energy, retail and public sector. Expect regulated-industry delivery, data-residency requirements under PDPL, and a client base where Arabic-language proficiency is an asset, though not a strict requirement. Job responsibilities - Shaping the bet. Running concept sprints with client executives, product managers and designers. Turning a broad ambition into something scoped and testable. Agreeing what success looks like, and what would tell us to stop, before anyone writes code. - Winning the work. Partnering with account leads to shape technical narratives on new pursuits. Supporting the pod construct and 3/3/3 commercial arc with client leaders with a clear understanding of pricing parameters. Owning technical scope in proposals, presenting confidently, and maintaining focus when discovery reveals core project requirements. - Proving it. Setting the technical direction for prototyping: what to build, what to fake, what to buy, and what evidence each prototype needs to produce. Pairing with designers and engineers so prototypes can actually be tested with users. Standing up proper evaluation for anything AI-powered, including golden datasets, offline evals, human review, guardrails, and cost and latency budgets. - Landing it. Owning an architecture that ships in three months and stands up long-term. Establishing delivery systems around it: agentic workflows with human oversight, continuous delivery, test strategy, observability, security, and privacy by design. On larger initiatives, maintaining architectural alignment across streams so each can ship independently. - Advising. Serving as a trusted technology advisor to key stakeholders. Aligning technical options with business outcomes. Presenting to steering committees, facilitating executive workshops, and shaping new opportunities with client partners. - Developing team members. Pairing, reviewing code, and mentoring colleagues. Creating reusable practices to support team continuity. Mentoring engineers onto lighthouse projects and sharing knowledge broadly across internal and external communities. Job Qualifications Technical Skills - Programming languages: Strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript, with working knowledge of the other, alongside experience shipping production code in at least one additional language. - AI & LLM ecosystems: Hands-on experience with major LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex), RAG and vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Elastic), and agent frameworks (LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex). - AI evaluation & observability: Proficiency in offline/online evaluations, golden datasets, LLM-as-judge patterns, tracing, and cost monitoring using tools like Braintrust, LangSmith, Langfuse, or custom harnesses. - AI-assisted development & prototyping: Active adoption of AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Replit) and rapid prototyping platforms (v0, Lovable, Figma Make) to accelerate delivery. - Cloud platforms & DevOps: Deep expertise in AWS, GCP, or Azure, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), containerization (Kubernetes, Docker), and automated CI/CD pipelines. - Software architecture & integration: Solid foundation in API design, event-driven streaming (Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub), microservices, and integrating with enterprise legacy systems. - Data engineering & analytics: Experience with modern data platforms (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) and orchestration tools (dbt, Airflow, Dagster) to design architectures for AI workloads. - Frontend development & modern practices: Capability to build prototypes using React/Next.js, alongside engineering practices like TDD, pair programming, continuous deployment, and threat modeling (OWASP LLM). - Governance, security & compliance: Experience delivering under complex regulatory environments (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, Saudi PDPL, or EU AI Act) and high-security standards. - Regional & cross-cultural engagement: Experience delivering in GCC markets or international settings, with Arabic language proficiency or public advocacy (talks, open source, publications) being a strong plus. Professional Skills - Effective communication: Comfortable and clear when presenting to diverse groups, facilitating workshops, leading pitches, or writing documentation that remains impactful asynchronously. - Product-minded approach: Fluent in outcome-driven delivery, continuous discovery, hypothesis testing, and focusing on minimum lovable products over output alone. - Inclusive leadership and mentorship: Skilled at guiding, pairing with, and unblocking engineers, empowering team members from all backgrounds to grow and own their work. - Adaptability in ambiguity: Composed when facing complex challenges, transitioning seamlessly between strategic advisor and hands-on collaborator as needs evolve. - Collaborative feedback: Open to giving and receiving constructive feedback with empathy, continuously sharing knowledge across disciplines. Why you might like it here - High-impact visibility: Work on flagship projects that deliver meaningful outcomes, where your contributions gain wide recognition across client teams and industry spaces. - Global perspective and variety: Collaborate across diverse global markets, industries, and multidisciplinary teams, continually enriching your experience. - Hands-on technical depth: Stay actively engaged with technology leadership without sacrificing practical engineering judgment or hands-on innovation. - Shaping the future of AI: Help define best practices for AI-first product development at the intersection of technology, product strategy, and user experience. - Growth and inclusive culture: Define your own path with tailored coaching, support, and learning opportunities in a culture that deeply values diverse backgrounds, varied experiences, and potential. Your first year, roughly - By three months: You'll have led a lighthouse engagement through a full 3/3/3 cycle, and clients will be asking for you by name. - By six months: You'll be working across more than one market, with at least one story we're telling externally. - By a year: Other Tech Principals will be running this play with assets and coaching you gave them, and you'll have a voice on AI-first product innovation that reaches beyond Thoughtworks. - Growth and inclusive culture: Define your own path with tailored coaching, support, and learning opportunities in a culture that deeply values diverse backgrounds, varied experiences, and potential. Travel and location This is a KSA-anchored role. Expect regular time in Riyadh and other GCC client sites — roughly 40% regional travel — plus occasional global (:10%) for CXPD-wide gatherings, cross-region pursuits and knowledge sharing. Other things to know Learning & Development There is no one-size-fits-all career path at Thoughtworks: however you want to develop your career is entirely up to you. But we also balance autonomy with the strength of our cultivation culture. This means your career is supported by interactive tools, numerous development programs and teammates who want to help you grow. We see value in helping each other be our best and that extends to empowering our employees in their career journeys. Crucially, our AI tools do not screen, assess, rank or make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team and all selection decisions are made exclusively by our interviewers and hiring managers. We are committed to fairness and responsible AI. We actively manage our AI systems by testing, monitoring for biased outcomes and implementing mitigation measures. The Foam Sculpturing / Fabrication Team Leader is responsible for overseeing the daily operations of the Foam Fabrication section in the event fabrication workshop, aiming at transforming raw EPS (Expanded Polystyrene) or polyurethane foam into detailed 3D props, scenic elements, and large-scale structures for corporate events, trade shows, theatrical sets, and themed attractions. The role involves interpreting design sketches or blueprints and using a combination of CNC-cut components and skilled manual hand-carving to produce visually stunning, durable, and lightweight props, ensuring that elements are fabricated efficiently, safely, and to high-quality standards. This hands-on role involves leading a team of foam fabricators, acting as the primary link between the production Managers /Designers and the workshop floor. Key Responsibilities 1. Team Leadership & Supervision • Lead, mentor, and motivate a high-performing workshop team to meet tight event deadlines. • Allocate daily tasks to team members based on project schedules and skill levels. • Provide training and support to staff, ensuring adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs). • Run daily, short "toolbox talks" or stand-up meetings to discuss project status, safety, and goals. 2. Production & Operational Efficiency • Blueprint Interpretation: Interpret technical drawings, 3D models, or artistic sketches and design to translate concepts into accurately scaled, physical props to guide fabrication. • Coordination: Coordinate workshop workflow to optimize production, reducing waste and downtime. • Foam Carving & Shaping: Carve, shape, and sculpt foam (EPS, PU) into 3D models using 3D robots, hot wire cutters, rasps, rotary tools, and hand saws. • Structural Assembly: Assemble multiple foam blocks, gluing, fitting, and clamping parts to create large-scale structures, ensuring structural integrity for transport and installation. • Detailing & Finishing: Apply fine details to foam surfaces using hand tools (e.g., Dremel tools) to create textures like wood grain, stone, or character features. • Surface Coating: Apply hard-coating materials (such as polyurea, epoxy resins, or sand-coat) to ensure durability for indoor/outdoor display. • Collaboration: Work closely with designers, painters, and welders to integrate steel armatures or electrical components into foam sculptures. Collaborate with project managers to update them on progress, potential delays, or material issues. • Support, and sometimes lead, on-site installation or load-in/out during high-pressure times. • Tool Maintenance & Safety: Clean and maintain specialized workshop machinery (3d robots and hot wires) and adhering to strict safety protocols and PPE requirements. 3. Quality Control & Safety • Enforce strict health and safety rules, including wearing PPE and maintaining a 5S compliant, orderly workspace. • Inspect finished products and assemblies for defects, ensuring they meet client specifications before leaving the workshop. • Identify and resolve technical fabrication issues early to prevent delays. 4. Material & Resource Management • Manage raw materials inventory and coordinate with purchasing for necessary items. • Ensure all equipment (saws, welders, routers, …) are maintained and in good working order.

DESCRIPTION_TEXT: We are recruiting an Energy Marshal for a major data center project in Riyadh (RUH-E-DC01). This is a safety leadership role with sole authority over the control, authorization, coordination, and supervision of all work on energized electrical systems during construction, testing, and commissioning. The mandate is clear: zero energization-related incidents, disciplined Lockout–Tagout (LOTO), and controlled first-time energization of MV and LV systems. The role You will be the single point of authority for energization and de-energization. You will coordinate OEMs, subcontractors, and the Commissioning (Cx) team, approve or reject Energized Work Permits, and hold Stop Work Authority where conditions are unsafe. Key responsibilities - Own the project Energization and LOTO Plan - Authorize MV/LV energization sequences and first-time energizations - Issue Notification of Energization (NoE) at least 24 hours in advance - Review and approve/reject Energized Work Permits - Validate LOTO procedures, PPE, and arc-flash boundaries - Confirm pre-energization checklists before any live work - Review commissioning scripts for energization risk - Maintain energized work logs, LOTO records, and permit files - Track and close SORs/NCRs related to energization - Enforce MOPs, OEM recommendations, and EOPs - Audit energized equipment and safety controls - Train the site on electrical hazards, arc flash, LOTO, and Permit to Work - Lead toolbox talks before high-risk electrical work - Investigate near-misses and incidents; drive root-cause and corrective action Must-have certifications - NFPA 70E — Electrical Safety Training - OSHA Electrical Safety Certification - LOTO / Hazardous Energy Control Training Who should apply Electrical safety professionals who have led energization on large construction or data-center / mission-critical projects. You must be comfortable holding the line on permits, LOTO, and first-time live work — and stopping the job when it is not safe. Location: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (project site — RUH-E-DC01) Phase: Construction, testing & commissioning To apply: Please email your CV, certifications, and a short note on relevant data-center / MV–LV energization experience. - Only candidates who can demonstrate hands-on authority over energized work and LOTO will be considered.

JOB_TITLE: Staff Product Manager - Shipping and Fulfillment
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: About the Role Over 100,000 merchants run their businesses on Salla, and every order they win ends the same way: something physical has to reach a customer. Shipping is where the platform stops being software. This role owns the shipping stack end to end and the economics underneath it: courier integrations, routing, cash-on-delivery reconciliation, exceptions, and partner performance, plus how far past last-mile delivery we go into inventory placement, warehousing, pick and pack, first-mile pickup, and returns. You lead a dedicated engineering squad as its one accountable product owner, and you own what a shipment costs and what the platform keeps on it. Few product roles let you own a merchant experience and its unit economics at the same time. This one does. You will drive impact across four major domains: Shipping Products (routing, label issuance, cash on delivery, tracking, driver-facing tools) Partner Integrations (provider onboarding, interface quality, status mapping, reconciliation, platform stability) Fulfillment Beyond Last Mile (inventory placement, warehousing and third-party orchestration, pick and pack, first-mile pickup, returns) Shipping Economics (carrier mix, rate card design, cost per successful delivery, what the platform charges and what it keeps) Responsibilities: Own the strategy and roadmap for shipping and fulfillment, prioritized on merchant retention and contribution per shipment, not feature count. Decide how each order is routed and priced: which provider carries it, at what service level, at what cost, and what the merchant pays. Raise delivery reliability where it is measurable: first-attempt success, service-level accuracy, exception rate, return to origin, and cash-on-delivery reconciliation. Build the integration layer that makes onboarding a new provider fast and keeps it stable once live: status mapping, retries, fallbacks, monitoring. Extend the product past last-mile delivery, choosing capabilities on merchant retention impact rather than on integration ease. Decide which shipping capability is free and which is paid, and defend where the line sits. Own the metrics with the data team, and move volume between providers when the performance data says to. Requirements Proven ownership of a shipping, fulfillment, or order-management product on a platform serving many businesses at once, with the numbers you moved: delivery success rate, service-level accuracy, exception rate, cash-on-delivery accuracy, or cost per shipment. Commercial fluency in shipment economics: you have built, priced, or renegotiated a rate card, and can explain how zone, weight, service level, cash on delivery, surcharges, and failed deliveries move cost per parcel. Depth past last-mile delivery in at least two of: inventory placement, warehousing or third-party fulfillment orchestration, pick and pack, first-mile pickup, reverse logistics, cross-border. Technical grounding in integrations: interfaces, webhooks, status mapping, retries, reconciliation. You can explain how a courier integration actually breaks and what made yours stable long term. Experience as the single product owner for a dedicated engineering squad, working across operations, commercial, and support rather than around them. Strongly preferred: you have built product on top of a partner network, where the company sold partner capacity and built its own capability alongside it. Seven or more years in product management. Full professional fluency in Arabic and English is required, and GCC logistics context is preferred over theoretical knowledge. Willing to relocate to Saudi Arabia.

JOB_TITLE: Resident Scholar (Local) - MCD, based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Riyadh
DESCRIPTION_TEXT: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The IMF Regional Office in Riyadh (ROR) is an office of the IMF Middle East and Central Asia Department (MCD) established in 2024 to deepen the Fund’s engagement with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and the broader Middle East and North African and Pakistan (MENAP) region. The office supports regional surveillance and capacity development through outreach and platforms for discussion among the region’s policymakers and other stakeholders. The Al-Ula Conference for Emerging Markets Economies (AUCEME), co-organized with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Finance, is ROR flagship event. ROR supports the IMF MENA Academic Conference series launched in June 2025 and contributes to the IMF GCC regional surveillance note. It is also developing an annual conference on financial sector issues with the Central Bank of Bahrain. ROR Resident Scholar is a position located in ROR premises in Riyadh. The Resident Scholar supports MCD’s analytical agenda by producing analytical work, e.g. drafting research papers and other analytical outputs, drafting and/or reviewing presentations for conferences and outreach events supported by ROR, and helping identify and mobilize speakers from academia and think tanks for these conferences, producing summaries of conference proceedings, compiling conferences’ key outputs into publishable documents (reports, books, pamphlets, etc.). The Resident Scholar reports to ROR director on administrative matters and to MCD’s Regional Studies Division (RSD) on analytical work. The Resident Scholar will work in collaboration with MCD policy groups and other IMF departments and aim to develop a network of economists and economic associations in the region. The position is for a duration of 6 months, renewable one time (starting as soon as possible) Objective of the Assignment This assignment offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the IMF’s regional engagement and enhance its impact through collaborative research. The Resident Scholar will play a pivotal role in deepening the Fund’s policy engagement in the GCC and MENAP. Administratively under ROR Director, the Resident Scholar will report to and develop his/her work program under the guidance of RSD and work with MCD policy groups and relevant IMF departments. The Resident Scholar will engage with regional academic institutions, think tanks, and associations of economists. The Resident Scholar will support ROR outreach and engagement on policy forums. Primary Objectives The Resident Scholar’s work will be anchored around the production of high-quality research aligned with MCD’s priorities. In addition to research outputs, the Resident Scholar will support the organization of the AUCEME and other ROR-supported conferences and policy forums. Strategic Contributions Beyond research, the scholar will actively support MCD ROR’s strategic pillars, which include: • Policy Forums: Supporting ROR senior policy forums and knowledge-sharing initiatives aimed at strengthening the region’s economic institutions and analytical capabilities. • Outreach and Engagement: Serving as a presenter or panelist at ROR-hosted events, to help disseminate research findings and foster dialogue on key regional issues. • Editorial Support: Under RSD’s oversight, editing or co-editing compilations of analytical work supported by ROR. Key Responsibilities • Conducts research on macroeconomic, fiscal, monetary, or structural issues as instructed by RSD and in collaboration with MCD policy groups. • Participates in regular coordination meetings with RSD and relevant MCD policy groups to ensure relevance, integration, and alignment with the HQ work program. • Helps identify and mobilize academic speakers for high-level events and conferences supported by ROR (e.g., Al-Ula Conference for EMEs, MENA Research Conference, high-level roundtables co-organized with regional institutions, etc.). • Contributes analytical notes, policy briefs, and background papers for regional events. • Participates as lecturer or panelist in policy forums and conferences supported by ROR. • Helps establish relationships with the economic faculties of key academic institutions and economic associations and think tanks. • Mentors ROR economists and contribute to internal knowledge-sharing. Qualifications • Ph.D. in Economics, Finance, or a related field. • At least 10 years of relevant experience in policy research, academia, or international organizations. • Demonstrated expertise in macroeconomic analysis, econometrics, or finance. • Strong record of publications in peer-reviewed journals. • Strong communication and drafting skills in English; Arabic is an asset but not required. • Familiarity with IMF operations and with MENAP economies are assets but not required. Interested candidates should submit (i) a curriculum vitae (CV), and (ii) a cover letter. This is a locally recruited position. Compensation will be based on the United Nations salary scale for the duty station.
